Creative and Media Widgets

  • Advanced Image Gallery: Organize images into customizable gallery layouts.
  • Audio Player: Add audio playback to your Elementor pages.
  • Creative Button: Style a call-to-action button with visual effects and icon options. Match the button treatment to the importance of the action.
  • Dual Button: Place two related actions together, such as viewing a demo and reading more information, without designing separate button layouts.
  • Flip Box: Display front and back content in flipping cards.
  • Hover Box: Reveal supporting text or links through an interactive box. Review the experience on touch devices as well as desktop screens.
  • Hover Video: Use a video preview in a portfolio or product presentation. Choose concise media and check its effect on page loading.
  • Image Accordion: Turn a group of images into expanding panels. Use it to introduce a small collection of categories, destinations or projects.
  • Image Compare: Place two images in a before-and-after comparison with a draggable divider. Use comparable images so the difference is easy to understand.
  • Image Expand: Create an expanding image presentation.
  • Interactive Card: Present content in an interactive card layout.
  • Interactive Links: Give navigation links an interactive visual treatment.
  • Lightbox: Open media in an overlay for closer viewing.
  • Lottie Image: Display Lottie animations within your design.
  • Marker: Highlight points of interest on an image.
  • Marquee: Present content in a scrolling marquee.
  • Remote Arrows: Place arrow navigation controls outside supported sliders.
  • Remote Fraction: Display fraction-style navigation for supported sliders.
  • Remote Pagination: Position pagination controls for supported sliders.
  • Remote Thumbs: Use thumbnails to navigate supported slides.
  • Slider: Present slides with supporting captions and buttons. Keep essential information easy to access instead of relying on visitors to see every slide.
  • Video Gallery: Organize multiple videos in a gallery.

Menu and Navigation Widgets

  • Circle Menu: Arrange navigation options in a circular menu.
  • Dropbar: Reveal additional content in a dropdown panel.
  • Mobile Menu: Add a mobile navigation layout with a menu toggle. Check labels, spacing and tap targets as part of your responsive review.
  • Navbar: Add a navigation bar to your page.
  • Off Canvas: Show supporting content in an off-canvas panel.
  • Scroll Button: Add a button for page scrolling.
  • Scrollnav: Connect a one-page menu to sections on the same page. This suits service pages and portfolios with clearly defined content areas.
  • Vertical Menu: Arrange navigation links in a vertical list.

Form and User Widgets

  • Contact Form: Add an enquiry form to your page.
  • Contact Form 7: Style forms from the Contact Form 7 plugin.
  • Everest Forms: Display and style existing Everest Forms.
  • Forminator Forms: Display and style forms created with Forminator inside Elementor. The Forminator plugin is needed for the underlying form functionality.
  • Mailchimp: Present a Mailchimp newsletter signup form.
  • Ninja Forms: Style forms created with Ninja Forms.
  • User Login: Add a user login form to your design.
  • User Register: Provide a registration form for new users.
  • WPForms: Display and style forms created with WPForms.

Marketing and Social Widgets

  • Countdown: Display a countdown for an event or offer.
  • Google Reviews: Display Google reviews in your website layout.
  • Review Card Carousel: Display review cards in a carousel.
  • Review Card Grid: Arrange review cards in a grid.
  • Social Proof: Present social-proof content in your layout.
  • Social Share: Add sharing options for your content.
  • Total Count: Highlight totals with a count display.
  • Twitter Grid: Present Twitter content in a grid.

Special Widgets

  • Age Gate: Display an age-confirmation prompt before selected content. An age prompt is not a substitute for any verification process your business may require.

Five Free Elementor Extensions

Extensions help you add detail to an existing layout instead of introducing another standalone widget. The free package includes these five options for supported Elementor elements and layout containers.

  • Backdrop Filter: Apply visual treatments such as blur and brightness to the area behind an element. Review text contrast when using translucent surfaces.
  • Grid Line: Add decorative grid lines to complement a structured page design. Use them selectively so they support the content rather than compete with it.
  • Ripple Effects: Add a ripple interaction to selected elements. A small response can help make an interaction feel more noticeable.
  • Tooltip: Provide short supporting information through a tooltip. Keep essential instructions visible in the main page content rather than hiding them only in tooltips.
  • Wrapper Link: Make a supported container or section clickable. Use it for a clearly defined destination and avoid confusing combinations of overlapping links.

Reusable Templates and Free Workflow Tools

Elementor Template Library

The Template Library gives you a starting point for page and section layouts. Import an available template, replace the sample content and adjust its appearance in Elementor. You can change text, images, colors, spacing and other editable settings to match the website you are creating.

Templates are starting layouts, not finished websites. Review each imported section for your own content, branding and responsive needs. Check whether a selected template uses premium widgets before relying on it in a free-only project. Template and widget availability should match the version you have installed.

Live Copy Paste

Reuse Elementor content across pages or supported sites with Live Copy Paste. Copy an existing design and place it where you need the same structure, rather than manually rebuilding its layout and styling. Enable the feature in settings before using the workflow.

Cross-site reuse is particularly helpful for repeated sections such as service summaries and calls to action. After pasting, review destination-specific text, links and images. Also check that the destination has the widgets and dependencies used by the original design.

Duplicator and SVG Support

Duplicator supports a repeatable workflow for posts, pages and templates. Use a duplicate as the starting point for a related page, then replace the content that should be unique. Before publication, check titles, links and any copied information that belongs to the original page.

Optional SVG Support allows SVG handling within the plugin’s supported workflow. SVG files are useful for scalable graphics such as icons and logos. Only upload files from sources you trust and review your site’s upload permissions before enabling additional file types.

Atomic Addons Pro: More Control for Complex Projects

The premium version expands the collection with 84 Pro Elementor widgets, 17 Pro design extensions and site-building features. Choose Pro when your project needs functionality beyond the free tools, such as dynamic post layouts, a visual theme builder or dedicated WooCommerce page elements.

You do not need to activate every premium feature at once. Select the modules relevant to the website, configure them and test the resulting pages. This keeps the editing workspace focused and makes it easier to understand which features a project actually depends on.

Advanced Content and Creative Widgets

Pro content widgets include Advanced Heading, Circle Info, Comparison List, Content Switcher and Price Table. Pro creative options include Animated Heading, Creative Gallery, Stacker and SVG Blob. Use them where a visual treatment helps explain or present the content.

Navigation and Mega Menu Builder

Atomic Addons Pro includes the Mega Menu, Sub Menu and Table of Content widgets. Create navigation that reflects how your website is organized, from a simple list of pages to a larger dropdown with multiple content areas.

The Elementor mega menu builder supports visual dropdown layouts. Use it to group related destinations and make a larger website easier to browse. After designing the desktop menu, review its mobile behavior and make sure important destinations remain easy to find.

Forms and Marketing Widgets

Pro includes the Webhook Form and the Facebook and Instagram feeds. Where an integration uses an external service, review its account requirements and configuration before adding it to a page.

Post Widgets and Dynamic Content

Present WordPress content through Post Grid, Post Carousel, Post List, Post Slider, timelines and other dynamic layouts. Instead of maintaining a separate manual card for every article, use post-based widgets to display content from your website.

Single-post elements include Post Title, Post Content, Post Featured Image, Post Info and Post …
atomic-elements.installation:
Install Through WordPress

  1. Make sure Elementor is installed and active on your WordPress website.
  2. Open Plugins > Add New in the WordPress dashboard.
  3. Search for Atomic Addons for Elementor and select the correct plugin.
  4. Click Install Now, then Activate.
  5. Open the Atomic Addons settings and enable the available modules you need.
  6. Edit a page with Elementor and find the enabled Atomic Addons widgets in the editor panel.
  7. Add a widget, configure its content and review the layout on different screen sizes.
  8. Save or publish the page after checking the result.

Installation activates the free package. Pro widgets and premium extensions require the separate Atomic Addons Pro upgrade. WooCommerce-specific tools also require WooCommerce to be active.

Manual Installation

Download the plugin ZIP from WordPress.org. In your dashboard, open Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, select the ZIP and install it. Activate the plugin after installation and confirm Elementor is active. If uploading extracted files through your hosting tools, the plugin directory remains named atomic-elements; that technical folder name is not the public product name.

Connect an AI Agent (Optional)

AI access is optional and off by default. The rest of the plugin works the same whether or not you enable it.

  1. Open Atomic Addons > AI in your WordPress dashboard and select Enable MCP access.
  2. Choose Read only or Read & write access, then select Turn on agent access. Read only is the default, and abilities that change your website stay unavailable until you choose Read & write.
  3. Select your AI client. Generate a setup prompt for the agent to follow, or copy a ready-made configuration: a terminal command for Claude Code, a configuration file entry for Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex or VS Code, or a standard server configuration for other MCP clients. Each client receives its own WordPress application password.
  4. Run the provided test prompt in your client and paste its answer back on the AI screen to confirm the connection.

To use Elementor’s Angie instead, install the Angie plugin and switch on the Angie integration under Settings on the AI screen. Angie then uses Atomic Addons tools inside the Elementor editor, with no external client or configuration file.

Requirements and Update Checks

The listing specifies WordPress 6.5 or later, PHP 7.4 or later and Elementor. WooCommerce is required only for WooCommerce-specific features. The optional AI features need WordPress 6.9 or later; external AI clients also need an active MCP Adapter and application passwords, which WordPress offers on HTTPS or local sites. Check the current plugin requirements before installation because supported versions can change as the software develops. Use a supported server environment and keep backups before major updates.
atomic-elements.faq:
What are Elementor addons?

Elementor addons are plugins that extend the Elementor page builder with extra widgets, templates or features. Atomic Addons adds content and design tools to Elementor, with optional premium features for dynamic websites, theme layouts and WooCommerce stores. It works alongside Elementor rather than replacing it.

Is Atomic Addons free to use?

Yes. The WordPress.org version is free and includes 78 widgets, five extensions and workflow modules such as the Template Library and Live Copy Paste. Atomic Addons Pro is an optional paid upgrade for additional widgets and premium functionality.

Do I need Elementor Pro?

You can use the free Atomic Addons plugin with the free version of Elementor. Elementor Pro is not required for that free package. Atomic Addons Pro is a separate product, so do not confuse its premium license with an Elementor Pro subscription.

What is the difference between Atomic Addons Free and Pro?

Free provides the core widget collection, free extensions and supported workflow tools. Pro adds advanced content, navigation, marketing and form widgets, plus Dynamic Tags, Display Conditions, Theme Builder functionality and WooCommerce tools. Check the feature’s Free or Pro label before planning a layout around it.

How do I add Atomic Addons widgets to Elementor?

Install and activate Atomic Addons, confirm Elementor is active and enable the desired widgets in the plugin settings. Open a page in Elementor, find the available widget in the editor panel and drag it into your layout. Premium widgets require the Pro version.

Does Atomic Addons work with every WordPress theme?

Atomic Addons is designed for Elementor-based websites and is intended to work with themes that support Elementor. Compatibility with every possible theme configuration cannot be guaranteed. Test your theme, template assignments and other plugins together on a staging site before making major live changes.

Can I use Atomic Addons with other Elementor addons?

You can use multiple addon plugins when your project needs features from different tools. Avoid unnecessary overlap and test the combination before publishing. If a conflict appears, reproduce it on staging and identify the specific widget, extension or setting involved before contacting support.

Will Atomic Addons slow down my website?

The plugin provides conditional asset loading and controls for disabling unused features. Actual performance depends on the complete website, including media, hosting, theme and other plugins. Measure representative pages before and after significant changes rather than assuming any addon has no performance impact.

Does Atomic Addons include Elementor templates?

Yes. The Template Library offers importable layouts that you can edit in Elementor. Enable the module, choose an available template and replace its sample content. Check whether the selected design uses premium widgets or other dependencies before using it on a free-only website.

Can I copy Elementor sections to another website?

Live Copy Paste supports reusing Elementor content across pages or supported sites when the feature is enabled. Review the copied section on the destination website and confirm that required widgets are available. Update any text, media or links that should differ from the original.

Can I create custom headers and footers?

Yes. Atomic Addons Pro includes header, footer and theme-building functionality. Design the layout visually and configure where it appears. Check mobile navigation and template assignments before applying a new header or footer throughout the website.

Does Atomic Addons support dynamic content and ACF?

Pro includes Dynamic Tags for supported content sources, including Advanced Custom Fields. Use them to connect compatible design settings to stored data. You need the relevant content, custom fields and dependencies configured before a dynamic layout can display the expected information.

Can I customize WooCommerce pages with Elementor?

Atomic Addons Pro provides WooCommerce widgets for products, catalogs, cart, checkout and account-related layouts. WooCommerce must be installed and active. Test the completed store with your payment methods and other extensions before publishing changes to purchase-related pages.

Are the WooCommerce extensions included in the free plugin?

No. The WooCommerce extensions described here require Atomic Addons Pro. They include Variation Swatches, Quick View, Wishlist, Compare and other store tools. Installing the free WordPress.org package alone does not unlock those premium extensions.

Do form integration widgets replace form plugins?

No. Widgets for tools such as Forminator, WPForms and Contact Form 7 work with those plugins. Install and configure the relevant form plugin first, then use its compatible Atomic Addons widget to display or style the form in Elementor.

Can beginners use Atomic Addons without coding?

Most visual widget configuration happens through Elementor controls, making the plugin suitable for users who prefer a visual editor. More advanced tasks, such as custom JavaScript, webhooks or complex store rules, may require additional technical knowledge and testing.

Can I connect AI agents such as Claude, Cursor or Codex?

Yes. The built-in Atomic Addons MCP server works with Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex, VS Code and other MCP clients that support remote servers. Open Atomic Addons > AI, enable MCP access and follow the on-screen connection steps. The screen generates the setup prompt, command or configuration for the client you choose.

What is MCP?

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets AI assistants use tools offered by other software. Atomic Addons offers its page-building, page-management and widget tools through MCP, so a connected agent can create and edit Elementor content on your website instead of only suggesting text or code for you to copy.

What can an AI agent do with Atomic Addons?

The MCP server offers 31 abilities, registered through the WordPress Abilities API, in seven groups:

  • Page Building: Read a page’s element structure, build a complete layout in one step, add sections, columns and containers, insert Elementor and Atomic Addons widgets, change their settings, move or remove elements, undo the last change and regenerate Elementor CSS.
  • Page Management: Create Elementor pages and posts, as drafts by default, list existing content, update titles, page templates and featured images, publish or return a page to draft, and move pages to the trash or restore them.
  • Design System: Read the global colors, fonts and spacing of your Elementor kit so new layouts match the rest of the website.
  • Widget Management: List widgets, extensions and features, switch them on or off, count how often each widget is used and switch off widgets that appear in no Elementor content.
  • Plugin Information: Report the installed edition, module tiers and the WordPress, Elementor, PHP and WooCommerce environment.
  • Integrations: Review and update the API settings used by widgets, such as Google Maps, reCAPTCHA and Mailchimp. Secret values are masked when an agent reads them.
  • Maintenance: Clear Elementor’s generated CSS and the plugin’s cached widget data.

For example, ask for “a draft landing page for our consulting service with a hero section, three feature boxes, client logos and a call to action, using our site colors”. The agent reads your design tokens, checks which widgets are available, builds the layout and saves the page as a draft for you to review.

Is it safe to give an AI agent access to my website?

AI access is designed to be opt-in and reversible:

  • MCP access, the MCP endpoint and the Angie integration are all off by default.
  • Read only is the default access level. Abilities that change your website are unavailable until you choose Read & write.
  • An agent acts as the WordPress user it connected with, so it can only do what that account is allowed to do. Page management and site-wide tasks, such as switching widgets or changing integration settings, need an administrator account.
  • Each ability is labelled Read, Write or Destructive, and any of them can be switched off.
  • Turning off agent access revokes the application passwords created on the AI screen, so connected clients lose access.
  • Pages and posts that were not built with Elementor are never overwritten by a generated layout.
  • Removed pages go to the trash rather than being deleted permanently, and the most recent AI builder change on a page can be undone. Older versions remain in Elementor’s revision history.

Atomic Addons does not send your content to an AI service itself. Your AI client does, when the agent reads pages or settings, under that provider’s own terms. Review what an agent produces before publishing it, keep backups and try new AI workflows on a staging site first.

Does Atomic Addons work with Elementor’s Angie?

Yes. With the Angie plugin installed and active, switch on the Angie integration on the Atomic Addons AI screen. Angie can then use Atomic Addons tools inside the Elementor editor without an external MCP client or configuration file.

What do I need to use the AI features?

You need WordPress 6.9 or later, because the AI features use the WordPress Abilities API. External AI clients also need an active MCP Adapter, either the WordPress MCP Adapter plugin or a copy included with another active plugin, and WordPress application passwords, which require HTTPS or a local development site. The AI screen tells you if something is missing. Angie needs the Angie plugin. You also need access to the AI client you want to use, because Atomic Addons does not include an AI model or AI credits.

Are the AI features included in the free plugin?

Yes. The MCP server, the Angie integration and all 31 abilities are part of the free WordPress.org plugin. An agent can insert the Atomic Addons widgets switched on for your website; Pro widgets become available to it when Atomic Addons Pro is active.

Where can I find documentation or get support?

Use the official Atomic Addons documentation for setup guidance and feature instructions. For the free WordPress.org plugin, use its support forum. Include your plugin versions, a clear description and reproduction steps, but never post passwords, payment information or other private credentials publicly.

How do I keep Atomic Addons updated?

Check the Plugins or Updates area in your WordPress dashboard for available updates to the free plugin. Review release notes and keep a backup before updating. For Pro, follow the account and update instructions supplied with your premium license, and test important workflows after changes.

zen-mcp-bridge.description:
Zen MCP Bridge turns your WordPress site into an MCP server that Claude.ai can connect to. Once connected, Claude can inspect your site’s architecture in real time — plugins, database schema, source code, ACF fields, REST routes, cron jobs and more — so it can write plugins, debug issues and answer questions tailored to your exact setup.

Read-only by default. Claude cannot write, delete or modify anything unless you explicitly enable the opt-in write mode — and even then it can only work with drafts, allowlisted options, plugin toggles, caches and terms, with every action audited.

Features

  • Full OAuth 2.1 authorization server with PKCE (S256), dynamic client registration (RFC 7591) and auto-discovery (RFC 8414 + RFC 9728).
  • Bearer Token auth as a simpler alternative to OAuth — never expires.
  • Configurable OAuth token lifetime — 1 hour, 24 hours, 7 days or 30 days, plus an emergency “Revoke all tokens” button.
  • 25 read-only MCP tools covering site info, plugins, themes, post types, taxonomies, options, posts, database schema, structured table reads, files, code search, logs, hooks, ACF fields, users, menus, cron, transients, widgets, REST routes, Action Scheduler, WooCommerce and Elementor.
  • MCP resources (site snapshots at wordpress:// URIs) and canned prompts for site analysis, debugging and plugin writing.
  • Opt-in write mode (off by default): six scoped write tools — create/update DRAFT posts, update allowlisted options, toggle plugins, clear caches, create terms. OAuth sessions additionally need a write grant ticked on the consent screen; everything is audited. Deleting, publishing, user management and write SQL are never possible.
  • WordPress Abilities API integration (WP 6.9+): tools are discoverable by the WordPress AI ecosystem, admin-only. Stands down automatically when the official AI Provider for Anthropic plugin is active.
  • MCP specification 2025-11-25 compliant.
  • Rate limiting, path-traversal guards, credential redaction and clickjacking protection.
  • Apache + FastCGI compatible (Authorization header normalization built in).
  • Zero dependencies — pure WordPress, no Composer required.

Available tools

Read: wp_get_site_info, wp_get_plugins, wp_get_themes, wp_get_post_types, wp_get_taxonomies, wp_get_options, wp_query_posts, wp_get_post, wp_get_db_schema, wp_db_query, wp_list_files, wp_read_file, wp_search_code, wp_get_logs, wp_get_hooks, wp_get_acf_fields, wp_get_users, wp_get_menus, wp_get_cron_jobs, wp_get_transients, wp_get_scheduled_actions, wp_get_active_widgets, wp_get_rest_routes, wp_get_woocommerce, wp_get_elementor.

Write (only with write mode enabled): wp_create_draft_post, wp_update_draft_post, wp_update_option, wp_toggle_plugin, wp_clear_cache, wp_create_term.

External services

This plugin is a bridge to Claude.ai, the AI assistant operated by Anthropic. That is the entire purpose of the plugin: it turns your site into an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that Claude.ai connects to so it can read your WordPress data and help you build and debug your site.

What the service is and what it is used for: Claude.ai (Anthropic) is a third‑party AI assistant. You connect it to this plugin’s MCP endpoint from the Claude.ai app. Claude then reads your site through the plugin’s tools to answer questions, write code and debug issues tailored to your setup.

What data is sent, and when: No data is sent anywhere until you, as an administrator, connect Claude.ai to this site and authenticate (with the Bearer token or by completing the OAuth login). After that, data is transmitted to Claude.ai only in direct response to a request Claude makes, and only the data returned by the specific read tool it calls — for example site/plugin/theme information, post content, database query results (with credentials redacted), or source files under wp-content (with sensitive files such as .env, wp-config copies, keys and database dumps blocked). Options and query results have secret‑shaped values redacted, user passwords are never returned, and — unless you explicitly turn on the optional write mode — nothing on your site is ever modified. During the OAuth login flow the browser is also redirected to Claude.ai callback URLs (https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback and the app./www. variants) carrying a short‑lived authorization code. The plugin does not send any usage analytics or telemetry, and it does not contact Anthropic on its own — Claude.ai always initiates the connection.

Service terms and privacy policy: Anthropic Consumer Terms of Service — https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms ; Anthropic Privacy Policy — https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy ; Anthropic Usage Policy — https://www.anthropic.com/legal/aup
zen-mcp-bridge.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to wp-content/plugins/zen-mcp-bridge, or install it from your WordPress admin.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen.
  3. Go to Settings → MCP Bridge to find your endpoint URL and Bearer token.
  4. Flush rewrite rules once: Settings → Permalinks → Save Changes.
zen-mcp-bridge.faq:
How do I connect with a Bearer token (simplest)?

  1. In Claude.ai: Profile → Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector.
  2. Paste your MCP endpoint URL (shown on Settings → MCP Bridge), for example https://your-site.com/wp-json/zen-mcp/v1/bridge.
  3. Set the auth type to Bearer Token (or API Key) and paste the token from the settings page.
  4. Save. Bearer tokens never expire.

How does the OAuth 2.1 login flow work?

Claude.ai auto-discovers the OAuth server from the /.well-known/ URLs and opens a login page on your site, where an administrator clicks Allow Access. If Claude.ai asks for details manually, use the Authorization URL and Token URL shown in the OAuth (advanced) section of the settings page, any Client ID except the literal text “Bearer Token”, and the scope claudeai.

I get a 404 / rest_no_route error

Go to Settings → Permalinks and click Save Changes to flush rewrite rules, and confirm the plugin is active.

The Authorization header is always empty (Apache + FastCGI)

This is handled automatically. If it persists, add this line to your .htaccess:
RewriteRule ^ – [E=HTTP_AUTHORIZATION:%{HTTP:Authorization}]

How do I enable debug logging?

Define WP_DEBUG, WP_DEBUG_LOG (true) and WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY (false) in wp-config.php, then read wp-content/debug.log or use the wp_get_logs tool.

Is it safe?

By default, yes — everything is read-only: credentials are redacted, database reads are structured (no raw SQL — table and column names are whitelisted against the live schema and every value is parameterized), file access is contained within wp-content, and OAuth uses mandatory PKCE with single-use, expiring authorization codes. Write access exists only when an administrator switches on write mode, is limited to drafts, allowlisted options, plugin toggles, caches and terms, and every write is recorded in the audit log. Deleting content, publishing, managing users and write SQL are impossible regardless of settings.

How does write mode work?

Enable it under Settings → MCP Bridge → Write mode (off by default). The static Bearer token then gains write access; OAuth sessions must additionally tick “Allow write access” on the consent screen (the claudeai:write scope). Six scoped tools become available; drafts can never be published, options must be on an allowlist you control (site identity, code-execution and secret options are refused even if listed), and the plugin can never toggle itself off. Each write tool can be disabled individually and every call is audited.

How does this relate to the “AI Provider for Anthropic” plugin?

They point in opposite directions and can coexist: that plugin lets WordPress call Claude’s API; Zen MCP Bridge lets Claude.ai read this site. When AI Provider for Anthropic is active, Zen MCP Bridge automatically stops registering its tools as WordPress Abilities so the site’s AI surface has a single owner — Claude.ai access via the MCP endpoint is unaffected. The zenmcp_enable_abilities filter overrides this.

videowhisper-security-audit.description:
VideoWhisper Security Audit creates WordPress site health, exposure, vulnerability, integrity, readiness, and performance reports for site administrators. The plugin is designed to help administrators review site activity and configuration with AI agents or by using the built-in admin report.

The free plugin is read-only. It reports findings and does not perform cleanup, quarantine, updates, file changes, role changes, or other remediation actions.

Plugin homepage: https://promptaur.com/wordpress/security-audit/

Main features:

  • Admin Scan tab with queued scan processing, live progress, per-task status, resume/retry controls, scan date, report summary, and report findings.
  • Configurable scan execution mode: queued scans by default, or legacy synchronous scans for small/basic sites.
  • Importance-based scan modes: full, critical/high/medium, and critical-only.
  • Report filters for issues only or all check results, including passed informational checks when available.
  • JSON and plain-text Markdown report output.
  • Optional token-protected REST report endpoint.
  • Optional token-protected MCP endpoint for read-only AI-agent reports.
  • Optional WordPress 6.9+ Abilities for admin-only read-only security overview, vulnerability, exposure, integrity, readiness, performance risk, and Markdown audit reports.
  • Optional exposure of those abilities through the official WordPress MCP Adapter when installed separately.
  • Read-only integration with VideoWhisper AI Site Manager – Using ChatGPT Claude Codex when both plugins are active, including report reads and agent-friendly queued scan tools.
  • Separate REST and MCP enable/disable settings.
  • Generated local tokens with rotation controls and last-used metadata.
  • REST/MCP per-minute rate limiting and optional exact IP allowlist.
  • Admin scan cooldown, hourly scan limit, and separate agent scan cooldown.
  • Category toggles for security, integrity, performance, readiness, commerce, community, and backup checks.
  • Redacted AI report defaults, with optional exact version and path disclosure for MCP reports.
  • Optional WPVulnerability API lookups for installed plugin vulnerability data.
  • Disclaimers in the admin report and Agents tab about report limits, sensitive information, and third-party AI analysis.

Queued scans

Queued scanning is the default admin interface. It splits inventory, exposure, vulnerability, integrity, performance, and readiness checks into small AJAX-polled batches. This avoids browser, proxy, and PHP timeout issues on larger sites while showing progress and recent queue events. Failed tasks can be retried, and unfinished jobs can be resumed from the Scan tab.

Administrators that prefer the original one-request scan flow can switch Scan execution to “Synchronous legacy scan” in Settings.

Local checks

Security Audit currently checks local WordPress signals including:

  • Plugin and theme updates.
  • Inactive plugins.
  • Administrator account count.
  • Expected WordPress database tables.
  • Administrator role capabilities.
  • Upload directory writability.
  • Debug log file presence.
  • Git metadata in the web root.
  • XML-RPC availability.
  • Common homepage security headers.
  • Autoloaded option size.
  • Expired transient count.
  • WP-Cron disabled state.
  • Permalink structure.
  • Search engine visibility setting.
  • Privacy Policy page presence.
  • Basic WooCommerce page readiness when WooCommerce is active.
  • Optional WPVulnerability plugin vulnerability lookups.

Agent and API reports

REST and MCP endpoints are disabled by default. When enabled, Security Audit automatically generates local tokens. Anyone with a valid token can read the selected report until the token is rotated, so treat tokens as sensitive secrets.

The REST report endpoint supports:

  • key: generated REST token. A bearer token can also be used.
  • mode: full, important, critical, or changed.
  • report: issues or all.
  • format: omit for JSON, or use markdown for plain Markdown output.

The MCP endpoint supports read-only tools for security summary, vulnerability, exposure, integrity, performance risk, readiness, and Markdown audit reports. Tool arguments include mode and report.

When VideoWhisper AI Site Manager is active, Security Audit also registers agent tools for latest summary/report reads, synchronous scan refreshes for small sites, scan task discovery, queued scan creation, queue batch processing, queue status polling, and retrying failed scan tasks.

On WordPress 6.9+, administrators can also enable WordPress Abilities. These abilities are admin-only, read-only, and permission-checked with manage_options by default. They can optionally be marked public for the official WordPress MCP Adapter, which must be installed separately. Existing REST and MCP endpoints remain available and are not replaced.

Some sites use an OAuth, firewall, or bearer-auth layer that consumes Authorization: Bearer before the Security Audit route receives the request. If standalone Codex MCP bearer setup returns oauth_token_invalid or a similar upstream bearer-auth error, use the MCP path-token URL shown on the Agents tab instead of the bearer URL.

Endpoint protection controls include:

  • REST/MCP requests per minute per IP.
  • Separate agent scan cooldown.
  • Optional exact IPv4/IPv6 allowlist.
  • Token rotation.

Developer hooks

Security Audit exposes generic hooks that any plugin can use to extend scan data, reports, admin UI, and Site Manager integration:

  • vwsa_latest_snapshot filters the latest stored snapshot before reports use it.
  • vwsa_scan_settings filters normalized scan settings for a scan context.
  • vwsa_scan_inventory filters inventory data before findings are finalized.
  • vwsa_scan_findings filters findings before snapshot lifecycle metadata is saved.
  • vwsa_scan_queue_tasks filters task definitions shown and queued by the Scan tab.
  • vwsa_scan_queue_process_task processes extension-owned queue tasks without coupling the extension to Free internals.
  • vwsa_snapshot_before_save filters the completed snapshot before it is stored.
  • vwsa_snapshot_saved fires after a snapshot is stored.
  • vwsa_report filters built report output.
  • vwsa_site_manager_integration filters the Site Manager integration definition.
  • vwsa_admin_tabs filters admin tabs.
  • vwsa_admin_render_tab lets extensions render custom admin tabs.
  • vwsa_admin_scan_panel_after renders generic content after the scan panel.
  • vwsa_admin_findings_before renders content before findings.
  • vwsa_admin_finding_card_start renders content inside a finding card.
  • vwsa_admin_finding_actions filters per-finding action links.
  • vwsa_admin_findings_after renders content after findings.

Important limitations and disclaimers

Security Audit reports are informational only. Findings and AI-ready reports may be incomplete, inaccurate, outdated, or unsuitable for a specific site or legal situation.

Security Audit does not provide legal advice, compliance certification, professional security advice, malware cleanup, incident response, or a guarantee that a site is secure. Administrators should verify findings and consult an experienced security, technical, or legal provider before making important changes.

REST and MCP reports may expose sensitive operational information, including site configuration, component versions, possible vulnerabilities, paths, and other details. Enable agent endpoints only when you understand where the data will be sent and who can access the token.

Third-party AI agents may produce incomplete, incorrect, unsafe, or unsuitable recommendations. Review all recommendations before acting and do not perform destructive changes without backups and appropriate professional review.

This plugin is not a firewall, malware cleaner, legal compliance tool, vulnerability scanner guarantee, or replacement for backups, security monitoring, dedicated scanners, or experienced administrators.

External services

By default, Security Audit does not call external vulnerability services.

If the administrator enables WPVulnerability lookups, the plugin sends installed plugin slugs to the public WPVulnerability API at https://www.wpvulnerability.net/ to retrieve vulnerability data. No API key is required for normal component lookups. Responses are cached locally. See:

  • https://www.wpvulnerability.com/
  • https://docs.wpvulnerability.com/
  • https://www.wpvulnerability.com/privacy/
  • https://www.wpvulnerability.com/license/

During scans, Security Audit may also make a local HTTP HEAD request to the site’s own homepage URL to inspect response headers. This request is sent to the configured site URL, not to a third-party vulnerability service.
videowhisper-security-audit.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install it from the WordPress plugin screen.
  2. Activate VideoWhisper Security Audit.
  3. Go to Tools > Security Audit.
  4. Run a scan and review findings.
  5. Open the Settings tab to configure categories, default scan/report mode, scan limits, and optional WPVulnerability lookups.
  6. Open the Agents tab to enable REST/MCP endpoints, rotate tokens, view endpoint URLs, and copy setup instructions if you want read-only external report access.
videowhisper-security-audit.faq:
Does this plugin change my site?

No. It stores scan reports and scan queue state, but it does not perform cleanup, quarantine, updates, file edits, role changes, or remediation.

Is this a firewall or malware scanner?

No. Security Audit checks health, exposure, vulnerability, integrity, performance, and readiness signals. It does not claim to detect or remove all malware, block attacks, or guarantee that a site is secure.

Does the plugin send data to external services?

Only if you enable WPVulnerability lookups. That optional feature sends installed plugin slugs to WPVulnerability and caches results locally.

The plugin may also request your own homepage URL during scans to inspect response headers.

Are REST and MCP endpoints enabled by default?

No. REST and MCP report endpoints are disabled by default and must be enabled by an administrator from the Agents tab.

Is the MCP endpoint public?

The MCP endpoint can be reachable by URL when enabled, but report access requires the generated Security Audit MCP token. Anyone with the token URL or bearer token can read the selected redacted report until you rotate the token.

The Agents tab also supports a per-minute endpoint rate limit and an optional IP allowlist for REST/MCP access.

For Codex, the bearer-token setup is preferred when the WordPress site does not intercept bearer headers. If another auth layer handles bearer headers first, copy the path-token MCP URL from the Agents tab and add it with codex mcp add <name> --url <path-token-url>.

What is the difference between issues and all reports?

Issues reports hide passed informational checks and show current reportable findings. All reports include informational passed checks when available, such as a WPVulnerability lookup that returned no affected vulnerability for the installed plugin version.

Can AI agents safely fix findings?

The free plugin exposes reports and scan refresh tools, but no cleanup or remediation actions. AI recommendations may be incomplete, inaccurate, unsafe, or unsuitable for your site. Review all recommendations carefully and consult an experienced provider before taking important action.

auditae-ai-search-toolkit.description:
Connect Claude and ChatGPT to WordPress over MCP (Model Context Protocol). Pair this plugin with an AuditAE account, add the hosted AuditAE MCP server (https://auditae.app/api/mcp) to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP client, and ask for changes in plain English. The agent can list, read, draft, update and publish posts and pages, edit Yoast / Rank Math titles and descriptions, lay out pages in Gutenberg blocks, manage schema and FAQ schema, curate /llms.txt and compress images in place. You choose what it may do: read, create drafts, publish, or write SEO settings. Every change is logged with its previous state, and one click on the Connect tab disconnects it. MCP is part of the optional AuditAE service: MCP reads are free; edits are 5¢ each (25¢ for a designed page; compressing images adds 1¢ per 5), and new accounts get $5 of credit with no subscription.

Free AI search readiness, no account. The plugin is also a free AI SEO / AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) toolkit that makes your site easier for ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews to read, trust and cite. It works the moment you activate, whether or not you ever use MCP.

Built for Elementor. Elementor pages are read from Elementor’s own widget data, not the leftover copy in the post body, so the per-post checklist, Query Fan-Out coverage, the link checker and llms.txt all see what your visitors see. AI agents edit Elementor text in place, including Elementor 4’s atomic Heading, Paragraph and Button widgets, one-click internal links land inside your Elementor text widgets, and renaming an image updates it in Elementor image widgets too. On the block editor, synced patterns are read as part of every page that uses them, and AI edits keep FAQ and other blocks valid in the editor.

AI Readiness Score. One 0–100 number, with a letter grade, for how ready your site is to be read and cited by ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Google AI Overviews, computed from local signals: citation bots blocked in robots.txt, FAQ and Article schema coverage, Organization schema, AI-bot 404s, freshness and llms.txt. Every failing check says what to fix and what it’s worth, and a 7-day delta shows the score climb. A companion per-post checklist in the editor sidebar grades the post you’re writing on an answer-first opening, question-shaped headings, FAQ and structured data, depth and freshness.

1. AI Crawler Tracker. Identifies hits from ~30 AI crawlers — GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Bytespider, CCBot, Meta-ExternalAgent, Bingbot and more. See the AI bot hits that reached WordPress over the last 30 days (pages served from a page cache never reach the plugin, so treat it as a minimum; see the FAQ), a by-bot breakdown with last-seen times, daily activity, top crawled paths, CSV export and a Dashboard widget. A built-in robots.txt audit flags any tracked AI bot your robots.txt blocks. It answers what Google Search Console can’t: “Are AI engines actually reading my site?”

2. llms.txt Generator. Serves a live /llms.txt file at the root of your site, conforming to the llmstxt.org spec — a markdown manifest that helps LLM-powered tools find the right pages on your site. Builds defaults automatically from your public post types, with per-section customization, optional links list, and a one-click “Reset to defaults”.

3. Schema Graph. Schema.org JSON-LD without touching your theme. Free, with no account: a site-wide Organization block you fill in once on the Schema tab; per-post Article, Blog post, HowTo or Product schema from the Schema box in the editor (blank fields fall back to the post’s title, excerpt and author, dates, URL and image are filled in on save, and a preview shows the exact JSON-LD); and per-post FAQPage schema from the FAQ box. On a paired site, AEBOT does the same in bulk and adds BreadcrumbList. Designed to coexist with Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO and SEOPress: AuditAE defers the types your SEO plugin already emits (Organization, Article), leaves Product to WooCommerce on product pages, and never outputs duplicate structured data. If your SEO plugin emits no Organization at all, AuditAE fills the gap with the one you saved; if your theme or another plugin already outputs one, AuditAE holds yours back.

4. IndexNow auto-ping. When you publish or update a post, the plugin notifies the IndexNow API so Microsoft Bing, Yandex, Seznam.cz, Naver, Yep and Amazon learn the URL changed instead of waiting to discover it (Google does not use IndexNow; Bing’s index also grounds AI answers such as Copilot’s). Changed URLs are queued and sent in batches a couple of minutes later, so a bulk edit or an import costs a few requests, not one per post. The site key is generated and served automatically, password-protected and noindex posts (Yoast, Rank Math, SEOPress, AIOSEO) are skipped, submissions pause on staging sites and while search engines are discouraged, and “Submit all published URLs” seeds the index in one shot.

5. Image filename rename. A “Rename file” action in the Media library turns a generic IMG_4821.jpg into a descriptive, keyword-bearing red-running-shoes.jpg — the filename is one of the few image-SEO signals AI engines and image search actually read. It renames the original and every generated thumbnail size in one move, then rewrites the old URL to the new one in your existing posts, Elementor pages and page settings, block widgets, theme header images, and the social-share images set in Yoast, Rank Math or SEOPress, so your live images, srcset and share cards never break. Free, no account, gated by your normal WordPress permissions.

6. Query Fan-Out coverage. AI engines split the reader’s question into 8–12 parallel sub-queries, retrieve one passage per sub-query and assemble the answer from those passages, so citations are won passage by passage. A panel under the editor models the fan-out for the post you’re writing (from your focus keyword, categories, titles and Organization schema; nothing leaves your site), splits your draft at its headings and shows which sub-queries each passage answers. Missing ones sort to the top, so “add more depth” becomes “you never say what this costs”. It scores five of the six documented fan-out types (implicit, comparative, entity-expanded, related, personalized); reformulation can’t be scored honestly (see the FAQ). Free, offline, no account.

7. Broken internal links + orphaned content. The Links tab lists links in your content that point at pages of your own that no longer resolve, a dead end for a crawler. Rank Math charges for a broken link checker in PRO; Yoast removed theirs. This one runs on your own site with no external requests and is deliberately conservative: archives, custom post types, files, paginated URLs, ?p= shortlinks and redirected paths are resolved before anything is called dead. Links to drafts, private or trashed posts are listed separately. Orphaned content is the other end of the problem: every published post and page nothing else links to. Pick one and AuditAE shows which of your pages already mention it in ordinary prose and links the phrase in one click, changing nothing else. The link graph rebuilds in the background after your edits, so the tab opens without waiting and says when a rebuild is still running. Both are Premium features in the big SEO plugins; here they’re free.

8. Redirects (AI-bot 404 → 301). When an AI crawler asks for a page that no longer exists, the Redirects tab lists that dead URL so you can 301 it to the page that replaced it, so the bot lands somewhere useful and the old URL’s link credit isn’t lost. Suggestions come straight from the AI crawler log, and scanner probes (.env, .git, wp-config backups) are left out. You can also add your own 301 or 302 rules, or start one from a dead path on the Links tab. A rule only fires on a URL that returns 404, so it can never hijack a page that still exists, and each rule counts its hits. Free, no account.

Plus FAQ schema injection. Add question-and-answer pairs to any post or page from the FAQ schema box in the editor — free, no account — and AuditAE publishes them as a schema.org FAQPage <script type="application/ld+json"> block on the post view. The pairs live in post_meta; your post content is not modified, and removing them is one click. If the post already gets FAQPage schema from somewhere else (a Yoast, Rank Math, All in One SEO or SEOPress FAQ block, an Elementor Accordion or Toggle with its FAQ Schema switch on, or Rank Math’s Schema Builder), AuditAE stands down so the page never carries two FAQPage nodes, and the AI Readiness Score counts the post as covered.

No external service is required for any of the above. All data is stored locally — crawler hits in one small dedicated table (90-day retention, dropped on uninstall), everything else in wp_options. No telemetry.

Optional — pair with AuditAE (auditae.app). AuditAE is a separate paid service that measures whether AI engines cite your brand for the prompts your buyers ask. Pairing lets its assistant (AEBOT) also draft and update posts, edit Yoast/Rank Math meta, manage the schema graph, curate /llms.txt, and rename, describe and compress your images in bulk (in place, originals kept). On sites running the companion AuditAE AI Autopilot theme it can also edit page copy, brand colors and structured records, and your wp-admin dashboard shows live AI-citation, Analytics and Search Console figures. Pairing is optional; everything above stays free. $5 free credit at signup, no subscription.

External Services

This plugin connects to two external services: IndexNow, and AuditAE when you pair the site. It also downloads images from URLs AuditAE supplies, as described below.

IndexNow (https://api.indexnow.org) — On by default; toggle off any time.
When the IndexNow feature is enabled, the plugin notifies the IndexNow API after you publish or update a public post or page (changed URLs are queued and sent together a couple of minutes later) and when you click “Submit all published URLs”. Nothing is sent from staging or development sites, or while Settings → Reading discourages search engines. Each request sends only: the URL(s) that changed, your site’s hostname, and a randomly generated site-ownership key (served as a verification file at your site root). No post content, personal data, analytics, or telemetry is transmitted. IndexNow is an open protocol operated by the participating search engines (Microsoft Bing, Yandex, Seznam.cz, Naver, Yep and Amazon); one submission notifies all of them. You can turn auto-ping off under Settings → AuditAE → AI Crawlers.

  • IndexNow documentation: https://www.indexnow.org/documentation
  • Bing terms of use: https://www.bing.com/webmaster/help/indexnow-faq

AuditAE (https://auditae.app) — Optional, opt-in only.
The free features (AI Readiness Score, crawler tracker, llms.txt, schema graph and the per-post Schema box, FAQ schema, internal links, broken link checker, redirects, image renames, Query Fan-Out coverage, IndexNow) do not call AuditAE. The broken link checker and Query Fan-Out coverage make no network requests of any kind — both resolve entirely against your own database. The plugin only contacts AuditAE after you pair the site from the “Connect to AuditAE” tab — in three ways. The first two are authenticated over HTTPS with the per-site bearer token you can revoke from the admin at any time:

  1. Inbound (AuditAE → your site). The AuditAE service sends authenticated REST API requests to this site to read posts, write drafts, manage schema, or update SEO metadata — only for the capabilities you grant. With the read permission it can also fetch the site’s status (site name and address; the WordPress, PHP and AuditAE plugin versions; the active theme’s name and version; the list of active plugins; and the permissions you granted) and the plugin’s own logs: the log of AuditAE actions on this site (including the previous state kept so recent changes can be undone) and the AI crawler log (bot name, path, response status and time; no visitor IP addresses). With the write SEO permission it can also compress images in place: it reads each JPEG, PNG or WebP image and its thumbnail files (from their URL, or through this API) and sends back smaller files of the same type and name; the plugin keeps the originals in wp-content/uploads/auditae-originals/, and Restore original in the Media Library puts them back.
  2. Outbound (your site → AuditAE). On a paired site, the AuditAE widget on the wp-admin Dashboard (and the companion AuditAE AI Autopilot theme’s dashboard, if you use it) requests a small scorecard from https://auditae.app/api/wp/summary to show your AI-citation rate, Google Analytics, and Search Console figures in one place. The request runs in the background (WP-Cron) when the widget or the plugin’s settings page is opened and the local copy is more than ~15 minutes old, so wp-admin never waits on it. Each request transmits only your site URL and the bearer token; the response is your own data, and the last copy is kept locally to display. If AuditAE answers that the pairing is no longer valid, the plugin shows a re-pair prompt instead. No post content, analytics, or telemetry is sent.
  3. Image imports. When a paired AuditAE account adds an image to your Media Library (for example, one you uploaded in AuditAE), your site downloads it from the source URL AuditAE provides, using WordPress’s HTTP API (wp_safe_remote_get()), which stops downloading once the file passes the size limit. That request sends nothing but the HTTP request itself; the file is type-checked before it is saved.

Links to auditae.app — Only when you click them.
A few links in the plugin’s own screens open auditae.app in your browser: the free AI citation check (Score tab and Dashboard widget) and Help & docs, which appear whether or not the site is paired; on the Connect tab, AuditAE sign-up and sign-in links that open AuditAE’s connect page with your site’s address filled in, and on a paired site the MCP setup link; and on a paired site the fix buttons that open AEBOT. Nothing is sent when the page loads; a link sends only what is in its URL, and only when you click it. The citation-check link carries your site name and domain to fill in the form, and the check runs only when you press its button on auditae.app. The AEBOT buttons carry the request and your site’s address; AuditAE opens the chat on this site with that request typed in. Nothing is sent to AEBOT or charged until you press Send, and AEBOT’s replies use your AuditAE credit.

  • Terms of service: https://auditae.app/terms
  • Privacy policy: https://auditae.app/privacy

The admin UI uses the Newsreader typeface, which is bundled locally in assets/fonts/ under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. No font requests are made to Google or any third party.
auditae-ai-search-toolkit.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Go to Settings → AuditAE. You’ll land on the AI Readiness Score tab — a 0–100 grade, with a letter grade and 7-day trend, of how ready your site is to be read and cited by AI engines, with a one-click fix on every check that isn’t passing yet.
  3. Open the AI crawlers tab to see which AI bots are reading your site (hits populate automatically as they crawl) and whether your robots.txt is blocking any citation engines like GPTBot, ClaudeBot, or PerplexityBot.
  4. Visit the llms.txt tab to review or edit the manifest served at https://example.com/llms.txt.
  5. (Optional) Visit the Connect to AuditAE tab to pair with an AuditAE account if you want the citation-audit and AEBOT writing features. Pairing needs a free AuditAE account; the tab links to sign-up with your site’s address filled in, then you generate a pairing code and paste it into AuditAE.
  6. (Optional) Connect Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor over MCP. Once the site is paired, the Connect tab shows the AuditAE MCP server address, https://auditae.app/api/mcp. In Claude or ChatGPT, add it as a custom connector and sign in with your AuditAE account. In Claude Code, Cursor and other clients that take a config file, use an API key from your AuditAE dashboard (the Connect tab links to the setup steps). Then ask your assistant to list your WordPress sites to check the connection.
auditae-ai-search-toolkit.faq:
Do I need an AuditAE account to use the plugin?

No. The AI Readiness Score, the AI Crawler Tracker and robots.txt audit, the llms.txt generator, Organization schema, the per-post Schema box (Article, Blog post, HowTo, Product) and FAQ schema box, the broken link checker, orphaned content and internal link suggestions, Redirects, image file renames, IndexNow and Query Fan-Out coverage are all free and standalone. They work the moment the plugin is activated, and pairing doesn’t take any of them away. The Connect to AuditAE tab is optional and only relevant if you want the paid citation audits, AEBOT, or MCP access for Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor.

Why does the broken link checker miss some dead links?

By design. It only reports links it can prove are dead, because the fix a user applies to a false positive is deleting a link that was working. Anything it can’t positively classify is left out of the report rather than guessed at. It also checks internal links only — external link checking needs real HTTP requests to other people’s servers, which is a separate feature with its own throttling and failure modes.

Are the fan-out sub-queries the real ones Google ran?

No, and the panel says so. Query fan-out is probabilistic and Google doesn’t publish the sub-queries it generates, so nobody can show you the exact set — every tool in this space either models them or asks an LLM to guess. AuditAE models them from your own site: your focus keyword, your categories, your post titles, and your Organization schema. The wording won’t match Google’s, but the themes do, and that’s what decides whether a passage of yours can be retrieved. Nothing is sent off your server to produce them.

Why do reformulations like “what is X” never appear in the list?

Because they can’t be scored honestly. A reformulation restates your seed topic in different words, so there’s no distinguishing term to look for — any on-topic post covers it by construction. Including such a row would mean either always passing it (meaningless) or reporting a post that opens with a textbook definition as missing its own definition (wrong). The gaps that matter live in the other five fan-out types, so those are what the panel shows.

Which AI bots does the Crawler Tracker identify?

GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, OAI-AdsBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-Web, anthropic-ai, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Bytespider, CCBot, cohere-ai, Diffbot, FacebookBot, Meta-ExternalAgent, Meta-ExternalFetcher, Bingbot, YouBot, Amazonbot, DuckAssistBot, PetalBot, TimpiBot, MistralAI-User, AI2Bot, iaskspider, AwarioRssBot and AwarioSmartBot. The list is curated to AI engines; we deliberately exclude Googlebot because that’s already covered by Google Search Console. Google-Extended and Applebot-Extended aren’t on it because they aren’t crawlers: they’re robots.txt tokens that Googlebot and Applebot read to decide whether your content may be used for AI, so no request ever carries them. The robots.txt audit still checks both.

Why does the crawler log show fewer hits than my server logs?

Because the plugin only sees requests that reach WordPress. A page cache (WP Rocket, LiteSpeed Cache, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, your host’s cache, or a CDN such as Cloudflare) answers many requests before WordPress loads, and those hits are never logged. Treat the counts as a minimum: if a bot shows up at all, it is reading your site. For fuller counts, add the AI bots’ user agents to your cache’s list of user agents it never caches (WP Rocket: “Never Cache User Agent(s)”; LiteSpeed Cache: “Do Not Cache User Agents”; W3 Total Cache and WP Super Cache: “Rejected User Agents”): GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-User, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot and Perplexity-User. A CDN needs the same exception as a cache-bypass rule on its side. Those bots’ requests then run through WordPress, which costs a little more server time.

Will the plugin slow down my site?

No. Crawler detection is a single substring scan of the User-Agent on template_redirect; only a matching AI bot adds one row to a small indexed table, which is kept to 90 days and capped at 200,000 rows by a daily background clean-up, never inside a visitor’s request. A 404 that matches none of your redirects is answered without loading the redirect list. The /llms.txt response is cached in a transient and regenerated only when you save changes. Schema injection runs once per page render in wp_head. IndexNow pings are batched and sent from one background event. On any reasonable host, the per-request cost is well under a millisecond.

Where is data stored?

Locally, on your own site — no telemetry. Apart from IndexNow pings (changed URLs only; on by default, see External Services), nothing leaves your site unless you pair it with AuditAE. AI crawler hits live in one small custom table, {prefix}auditae_crawler_hits (pruned to 90 days and 200,000 rows, dropped on uninstall); everything else is in wp_options: auditae_crawler_rollup (per-bot first-seen + lifetime totals), auditae_redirects (redirect rules) and auditae_redirect_sources (an index of their source paths), auditae_audit_log (action log for the optional Connect tab), auditae_llms_txt_config (llms.txt manifest), auditae_organization_schema (site-wide schema), auditae_score_history / auditae_score_best (AI Readiness Score trend), auditae_score_email (the optional digest opt-in), auditae_link_index (the internal link graph), and IndexNow settings and its queue of changed URLs waiting to be sent — plus per-post meta _auditae_schema_graph and _auditae_faq_schema. On paired sites that used image compression, the original images AuditAE replaced are kept as files in wp-content/uploads/auditae-originals/, recorded in _auditae_media_backup post meta. That folder carries a deny-all .htaccess; nginx ignores .htaccess, so on nginx add location ^~ /wp-content/uploads/auditae-originals/ { deny all; } to your server block to keep it private. Uninstalling removes all of it except those originals, because they are the only copy of your images as they were: restore them first (Media Library → Restore original), or delete the folder yourself if you don’t need them.

What does the AuditAE connection cost?

Pairing is free. AuditAE itself is pay-per-use: AI-engine checks cost 5¢–12¢ each depending on the engine, WordPress edits cost 5¢ each (25¢ for a designed page; compressing images adds 1¢ per 5 images), and reads are free. Replies from AEBOT, the AuditAE assistant, are billed per reply on the AI tokens they use, and each reply shows its exact charge. New accounts get $5 of credit and there is no subscription. Sign up at https://auditae.app.

How do I revoke the AuditAE connection?

Settings → AuditAE → Connect to AuditAE tab → Disconnect. The bearer token is wiped instantly.

Does AuditAE conflict with Yoast SEO, Rank Math or other SEO plugins?

No — it’s designed to run alongside Yoast SEO, Rank Math, All in One SEO, SEOPress and The SEO Framework. AuditAE is an AI-search toolkit, not an SEO plugin: it never outputs title tags, meta descriptions, canonical URLs, Open Graph tags or sitemaps of its own, so it won’t trigger a “you have two SEO plugins active” warning. It changes values your SEO plugin stores only when asked: AEBOT can edit a post’s SEO title and description with your permission, and renaming an image updates the social-image URLs your SEO plugin saved, so share cards don’t break. Where the two genuinely overlap — structured data and IndexNow — AuditAE detects your SEO plugin and steps aside:

  • Schema: it leaves the node types your SEO plugin owns (Organization, WebSite, Article, BreadcrumbList…) to that plugin and adds only the types it doesn’t cover, such as HowTo or Product, so you never get duplicate JSON-LD. The one exception: if your SEO plugin demonstrably emits no Organization or Person node and you’ve saved one in AuditAE, AuditAE emits yours so the site isn’t left without a publisher entity.
  • FAQ schema: it skips posts that already carry an SEO plugin’s FAQ block, or Rank Math Schema Builder FAQ schema.
  • IndexNow: it turns its auto-ping off if Rank Math (or a standalone IndexNow plugin) is already submitting.

You keep AuditAE’s AI-specific features — crawler tracking, AI Readiness Score, llms.txt — on top of your existing SEO setup, and a note on the plugin’s own settings page says exactly what’s been deferred.

How do I connect Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor to my WordPress site?

Pair the site on the Connect to AuditAE tab (a free AuditAE account is needed), then add the AuditAE MCP server, https://auditae.app/api/mcp, to your AI client. In Claude or ChatGPT, add it as a custom connector and sign in with your AuditAE account; that one connection covers every paired site in your workspace. In Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf and other clients that take a config file, connect with an API key from your AuditAE dashboard; team workspaces connect with an API key too. The assistant can then read, draft, edit and publish posts, edit SEO titles and descriptions, and manage schema and llms.txt, limited to the permissions you granted on the Connect tab. MCP reads are free; edits are 5¢ each (25¢ for a designed page). Every change is listed on the Activity tab, and Disconnect revokes access at once.

What is IndexNow and do I need to set it up?

IndexNow is an open protocol that lets your site tell search engines “this URL just changed” instead of waiting for them to re-crawl on their own. The participating engines are Microsoft Bing, Yandex, Seznam.cz, Naver, Yep and Amazon, and one submission reaches all of them. Bing’s index also feeds AI answers such as Copilot’s, so faster indexing means faster eligibility to be cited. There’s nothing to set up — the plugin generates and serves the required ownership key automatically, and starts pinging on your next publish. It pauses on its own on staging and development sites and while Settings → Reading → “Discourage search engines from indexing this site” is ticked. To turn it off, go to Settings → AuditAE → AI Crawlers and uncheck auto-ping. Google does not use IndexNow (it has no public submission API), so this complements rather than replaces normal Google crawling.

shim-mcp.description:
Shim MCP is a self-contained MCP (Model Context Protocol) server plugin for WordPress. It provides 56 abilities that let any MCP-compatible AI client manage your WordPress site — posts, pages, media, users, plugins, menus, widgets, comments, options, and system settings. The MCP server and every ability ship in the one plugin, so no companion plugins are required.

The MCP protocol layer is derived from the WordPress project’s own MCP Adapter (GPL-2.0), and abilities are registered through WordPress’s Abilities API, which core ships from 6.9. See the Credits section below.

Key features:

  • 56 WordPress abilities organized across 9 domains
  • MCP protocol v2025-06-18 with SSE transport
  • Admin dashboard with API key generation
  • Config export for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, and Cursor
  • Conflict detection for legacy MCP plugins

Credits

Shim MCP builds its MCP protocol layer on two GPL-2.0 projects published by the WordPress project:

  • WordPress MCP Adapter – everything under includes/Server/ (transport, JSON-RPC routing, session management, tools/resources/prompts handlers, schema transformation, error and observability infrastructure) is derived from it.
  • WordPress Abilities API – every ability is registered through this core API, which WordPress ships from 6.9.

The 56 abilities, the admin dashboard, the WP-CLI stdio bridge and the packaging are original to this plugin. Full breakdown in CREDITS.md.
shim-mcp.installation:
1. Upload the plugin zip file via Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, or clone the repository into wp-content/plugins/shim-mcp/.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu.
  3. Go to Tools > Shim MCP, generate an API key, and copy the config snippet into your AI client.
shim-mcp.faq:
What is MCP?

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that allows AI clients like Claude to interact with external systems through a structured protocol. It defines how AI tools discover and use capabilities (called “abilities” in WordPress) provided by a server.

Do I need MCP Adapter or the Abilities API installed alongside this?

No. Shim MCP is self-contained: it bundles its own MCP server, and the Abilities API it registers against is part of WordPress from 6.9 onwards. Nothing else is required.

Can it edit wp-config.php?

Only if you let it. The ability that rewrites the WP_DEBUG constants is switched off until you add define( 'SHIM_MCP_ALLOW_CONFIG_WRITES', true ); to wp-config.php yourself. Without that line the ability refuses, and it is refused again if DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT or DISALLOW_FILE_MODS is set, if the file is not writable, or if the rewritten contents fail a sanity check.

It warns me about another MCP plugin. Why?

Two MCP server plugins running at once can register competing abilities and endpoints, which produces confusing results for the connected AI client. If Shim MCP detects another MCP server or a standalone Abilities API plugin, it shows a notice suggesting you run only one. This is a compatibility warning, not a judgement about the other plugin.

What AI clients are supported?

Any MCP-compatible client works. The admin dashboard provides ready-made config snippets for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, and Cursor.

Do I need HTTPS?

HTTPS is strongly recommended for production use since API credentials are transmitted with each request. The plugin will work over HTTP for local development.

What WordPress capabilities are required?

Different abilities require different WordPress capabilities. For example, content abilities require edit_posts, user abilities require list_users or edit_users, and system abilities require manage_options. See the full abilities reference in docs/ABILITIES.md.

harudigi-booking-abilities-for-amelia.description:
HaruDigi Booking Abilities for Amelia and Easy MCP AI exposes seven meta abilities (help, status, discover, query, mutate, book, pay) so AI agents can manage Amelia without 100+ tools.

While active, this plugin unregisters Amelia Pro’s native abilities from the WordPress Abilities API so Easy MCP AI only sees the meta tools (natives duplicate coverage and hardcode approved on create). Amelia’s separate MCP HTTP endpoint is left alone; deactivate this plugin to restore natives.

Requires Amelia Booking 9.7+. Easy MCP AI is required.

Disclaimer: Independent plugin by HaruDigi — not affiliated with or endorsed by TMS Software.

What this plugin does

  • Registers 7 meta Amelia abilities for Easy MCP AI
  • Suppresses Amelia Pro native abilities in the Abilities API while active
  • Redacts secrets; blocks password / externalId writes
  • Requires confirm=true for deletes/cancels
  • notify defaults false; status follows Amelia defaultAppointmentStatus
  • Payment link URLs (Stripe etc.) via amelia/pay action=link

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.9+
  • PHP 7.4+
  • Easy MCP AI active (required)
  • Amelia Booking 9.7+ (required for abilities to run)

Updates

  • WordPress.org installs update from wordpress.org
  • GitHub / direct ZIP installs can update from public GitHub Releases

Author: Jens Madsen · Brand: HaruDigi · harudigi.com
harudigi-booking-abilities-for-amelia.installation:
1. Install and activate Easy MCP AI.
  2. Install and activate Amelia Booking 9.7 or newer.
  3. Upload the harudigi-booking-abilities-for-amelia folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install the release ZIP.
  4. Activate HaruDigi Booking Abilities for Amelia and Easy MCP AI.
  5. In Easy MCP AI → Abilities, confirm only the 7 meta amelia/* tools are enabled.
  6. Create a bearer token; connect clients to /wp-json/easy-mcp-ai/v1/mcp.
harudigi-booking-abilities-for-amelia.faq:
What Amelia version do I need?

Amelia Booking 9.7 or newer.

Is this an official Amelia / TMS plugin?

No. Independent HaruDigi plugin — not affiliated with or endorsed by TMS Software.

Does this replace Amelia’s MCP tools?

For Easy MCP AI: yes while active — Amelia’s 12 native abilities are unregistered from the Abilities API so agents only see the 7 meta tools. Amelia Pro’s own MCP HTTP route (/wp-json/mcp/...) is not configured by this plugin. Deactivate to restore natives.

Why is Easy MCP AI required?

Easy MCP AI is the MCP host. This plugin adds Amelia abilities to that host.

How do I book without emailing the customer?

Leave notify / notifyParticipants unset or false (the default). Only set true after the human approves. That flag only allows mail on create/status events — it does not send by itself.

How do I send a customer email for an existing booking?

amelia/book with action=notify (or resend), appointment id, and confirm:true. Optional booking_id. The matching customer status template must be enabled in Amelia → Notifications.

How do payment links work?

amelia/pay with action=link returns a checkout URL for the appointment’s remaining balance. Card checkout in a browser is out of scope for MCP.

revupnow-mcp.description:
Revi turns your WordPress site into a Model Context Protocol server, so an
AI assistant can work in your site directly instead of you copying text back and forth.

Connect Claude Desktop, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Gemini CLI or any other MCP-capable
client. Your AI can then read, create, update and publish content, manage media, edit pages in Elementor and
Gutenberg, handle taxonomies and comments, update SEO metadata, and work with WooCommerce products and orders –
all in natural language, and all inside permissions you set.

Works locally, with optional connected services

Install it, connect your AI client, and you are working. Every local MCP tool works without connecting the
site to RevUp Now.

The optional Account & Sync screen can connect the site to revupnow.ai. Nothing is sent before an
administrator explicitly starts and completes that connection. After connection, aggregate MCP usage and
WooCommerce customer contact sync remain active while the site is connected. Disconnecting the site stops both.

Usage reporting does not limit Lite

When enabled, usage reporting sends one daily aggregate: the number of completed MCP tool calls. Prompts,
arguments, results, WordPress users, URLs and IP addresses are not included. Reporting is analytics only;
it never caps, disables or unlocks Lite functionality.

Safety comes first

An AI that can edit your site is only reasonable if you decide what “edit” means. Every request is checked
several times over:

  • HTTPS is required. A request over plain HTTP is refused before anything else happens.
  • Two authentication methods – a static API key for CLI-style clients, or OAuth 2.1 with PKCE for clients
    that support it. Requests carrying neither are rejected.
  • Five safety modes – from Read Only, through Safe Editor, up to Full Access. The AI can never exceed the
    mode you pick, whatever it is asked to do.
  • Granular permission scopes – turn individual capabilities on or off independently of the safety mode.
  • WordPress capability checks – every tool declares the capability it needs, and it is checked against the
    connecting user on every call. An AI can never do something its user could not do by hand.
  • Administrator approval – require a human to sign off before destructive actions, or before anything is
    published.
  • A full audit log – every tool call, what it changed, and whether it was allowed.

The plugin never writes to WordPress core, to themes, or to plugin files. It works on content.

What your AI can do

  • Posts, pages and custom post types – read, draft, update, schedule and publish
  • Media library – upload, edit metadata, attach to content
  • Elementor and Gutenberg – read and edit real page structure, not just HTML
  • Taxonomies and comments
  • SEO metadata, including Yoast
  • WooCommerce products, orders and coupons
  • Read-only site status

Revi Pro

Revi Pro is a separate, paid plugin for people who want their assistant to reach
further than content:

  • Developer Mode – lets the assistant read and write your own theme and plugin files, and run read-only
    SQL against your database. WordPress core, wp-config.php and .htaccess are refused outright, and the
    plugin files it may touch are restricted to an allowlist you set.
  • Figma to WordPress – converts a Figma frame into a native page across five builders.
  • The AI Design System – builds and maintains a consistent design across a site.
  • Priority support.

None of that code is in this download. Not disabled, not hidden, not waiting behind a key – simply not
included, so there is nothing here to unlock and nothing extra running on your site.

External services

This plugin can connect to RevUp Now, operated by RevUp Now AI at https://revupnow.ai/.

No request is sent to this service until an administrator explicitly chooses to connect the site and
confirms their email. After connection:
