When you connect an external MCP client (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, etc.), the client connects directly to your site’s MCP endpoint. The plugin does not relay your data through any third-party server. The connection uses the credentials you generate in the plugin.
smarto-smart-mcp.installation:
1. Upload the smarto-smart-mcp folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install through the WordPress plugins screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen.
  3. Go to Smart MCP → Getting Started and add your AI provider API key.
  4. Click Test connection, then save.
  5. Open the Smart MCP chat and start asking.
smarto-smart-mcp.faq:
Which AI providers are supported?

OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), Google Gemini, OpenRouter and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Add your API key on the AI Providers page. Keys are encrypted at rest and never shown again.

What MCP clients can connect?

Any client that supports the Model Context Protocol, for example Claude Desktop, Claude Code or Cursor. Enable external access in Settings, generate an API key, then connect to https://your-site.com/wp-json/smart-mcp/v1/mcp (or use the discovery file https://your-site.com/wp-json/smart-mcp/v1/.well-known/mcp.json).

What can external MCP clients do?

External MCP clients are limited to non-administrative work: content, media, comments, menus, taxonomies and read-only site information. They never run as an administrator. Requests from an external client run as a non-administrative user who can edit posts (for example an Editor), so they cannot install, activate or update plugins and themes, manage users, change site settings or modify site code. External access is off by default and only works after you turn it on and generate a credential on the Connect page.

Is this safe?

Every available tool requires the appropriate WordPress capability, and actions that require approval must be explicitly approved before they run.

Can I chat from Telegram?

Yes. Set up a Telegram bot on the Telegram Bot page, and you can chat with your site from Telegram.

Does it work on multisite?

Not yet. Multisite support is planned.

Is there a Pro version?

Yes. Smart MCP Pro is an optional add-on that installs next to this plugin and adds tools for managing and maintaining the whole site. Nothing in the free plugin is locked or limited, and the free plugin keeps working the same with or without Pro. See the Free and Pro comparison.

uncap-ai-shopping-connector-for-woocomme.description:
Uncap AI Shopping Connector for WooCommerce connects your store to AI shopping agents. It implements the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP), ACP pre-flight discovery, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools. UCP and MCP agents can search products and create checkouts; ACP agents can detect the store and its currently advertised capabilities before attempting a transaction.

What this means in practice

AI agents like Claude, ChatGPT, and others are beginning to shop on behalf of users. When a user says “order me roses for my wife’s birthday,” the agent needs a structured way to find a store, check availability, and complete a purchase. UCP is the protocol that makes that possible. This plugin makes your WooCommerce store a first-class destination for those agents.

Features

  • UCP and ACP discovery — agents find and understand your store through /.well-known/ucp, /.well-known/acp.json, and REST discovery
  • Agent-ready catalog — AI-optimized product search plus per-product readiness scoring for the fields agents and feeds actually use
  • Agent checkout — create, update, and complete checkouts via REST, with fulfillment, coupons, and webhook support
  • MCP and WebMCP tools — a JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint plus browser tools for agents that search and initiate purchases
  • Local agent analytics — see protocol traffic, product searches, checkout progress, and completed orders inside your store
  • Conformance tested — zero failures or errors across the current 77-test official UCP suite (17 suites; 14 capability-dependent skips)

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.0+
  • WooCommerce 7.0+
  • PHP 8.0+
  • Pretty Permalinks enabled

External Services

This plugin connects to the following external services:

UCP schema and specification URLs

The plugin includes https://ucp.dev/ URLs in UCP discovery and schema response payloads as passive identifiers for the Universal Commerce Protocol specification. These values are not service endpoints used by the plugin. The plugin never connects to ucp.dev and never sends store, customer, order, or analytics data to ucp.dev.

The ACP pre-flight document includes https://agenticcommerce.dev/ as a passive documentation identifier for the Agentic Commerce Protocol. The plugin never connects to agenticcommerce.dev and never sends store, customer, order, or analytics data to it.

The plugin also includes passive schema identifiers from https://schema.org/ in front-end JSON-LD markup, https://json-schema.org/ inside the bundled local WebMCP library, and the standard http://www.w3.org/2000/svg XML namespace inside bundled admin SVG icons. The plugin does not connect to any of these domains or send data to them.

UCP Checker admin link

The admin dashboard includes a link to https://ucpchecker.com so store owners can learn more about the public UCP Checker service. The plugin does not call ucpchecker.com automatically and does not send store, customer, order, analytics, or installation data to it. Data is shared with ucpchecker.com only if a store owner manually opens that external site and chooses to use it. Terms and privacy policy are provided by ucpchecker.com on that external site.

AI agent webhook URLs

When an AI agent initiates a checkout, it may supply an agent profile URL in the UCP-Agent request header. When Agent Webhooks are enabled, the plugin fetches that profile URL to read the agent’s configured webhook URL. The plugin then sends order event notifications (e.g. order placed, order shipped) to that webhook URL. This feature is disabled by default and must be enabled by the store owner under Agentic Commerce → Settings → Agent Webhooks.

  • Data sent to the agent profile URL: the HTTP request needed to retrieve the public agent profile
  • Data sent to the webhook URL: the current order snapshot for the agent checkout, including checkout ID, order status, permalink URL, currency, line items, totals, buyer contact fields, adjustments, fulfillment expectations, and fulfillment events
  • When: only during an active agent-initiated checkout session, and only when the store owner has enabled webhooks
  • Who receives it: the AI agent service that initiated the checkout (e.g. Claude, a custom agent)
  • Opt-in: store owner controls this in plugin settings
  • Terms and privacy policy: the destination is supplied by the external AI agent service, so there is no single terms or privacy URL controlled by this plugin. Store owners should review that agent service’s terms and privacy policy before enabling Agent Webhooks.

Bundled JavaScript library

The WebMCP feature uses the @mcp-b/global library (MIT licence), bundled locally in assets/js/mcp-global.iife.js. No requests are made to unpkg.com or any CDN at runtime. Source code: https://github.com/WebMCP-org/npm-packages/tree/main/packages/global

The Checkout activity admin screen renders local charts with Chart.js 4.4.6 (MIT licence), bundled locally in assets/js/vendor/chartjs/chart.umd.min.js (unmodified npm UMD build). No requests are made to any CDN at runtime. Source code and build tooling: https://github.com/chartjs/Chart.js/tree/v4.4.6
uncap-ai-shopping-connector-for-woocomme.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress
  3. Ensure WooCommerce is installed and active
  4. Go to Agentic Commerce → Dashboard for a store status overview
  5. Check Agentic Commerce → Settings for your live UCP, MCP, and well-known endpoint URLs
uncap-ai-shopping-connector-for-woocomme.faq:
What is UCP?

Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) is an open standard that enables AI agents to interact with online stores. It defines how agents discover stores, browse product catalogs, create checkouts, and handle fulfillment. See ucp.dev for the full specification.

What is MCP?

Model Context Protocol (MCP) is a JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol that lets AI models call tools on external servers. This plugin exposes your WooCommerce store as a set of MCP tools, making it usable by agents like Claude Desktop without any custom code.

What is ACP support in this release?

Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP) agents can use the public /.well-known/acp.json pre-flight document to detect the store, protocol version, currency, locale, and currently supported services. ACP checkout is not advertised or implemented yet; UCP and MCP remain the transaction-capable surfaces.

Do I need to change anything about my store?

No. The plugin works with your existing WooCommerce setup — products, payment gateways, shipping methods, and order flows stay exactly as they are. The plugin adds a protocol layer on top.

Which AI agents does this work with?

Any agent that implements UCP or MCP. That includes Claude (via MCP), and any custom agent built on top of the UCP open standard. The protocol is designed to be agent-agnostic.

Does this replace my normal WooCommerce checkout?

No. Human customers continue to use your regular WooCommerce checkout. The UCP/MCP endpoints are an additional interface used only by AI agents.

Why are some REST endpoints public?

UCP, ACP pre-flight discovery, and MCP discovery/search endpoints are public so agents can inspect public protocol capabilities and catalog data before checkout. OAuth authorize/token endpoints are public protocol entry points: authorization requires a logged-in WordPress user and nonce-protected consent, while token exchange requires a one-time authorization code or refresh token stored server-side. Checkout/order follow-up routes use generated checkout UUIDs rather than sequential WooCommerce order IDs, so possession of the active checkout UUID is the protocol credential for that session.

What data is sent externally?

By default, nothing. If the store owner enables Agent Webhooks under Agentic Commerce → Settings, the plugin may fetch the agent profile URL supplied in the UCP-Agent request header to discover a webhook URL, then POST order status events to that webhook URL at checkout time. URLs under https://ucp.dev/ and https://agenticcommerce.dev/ appear only as passive protocol/specification identifiers in discovery response payloads; the plugin never fetches them and never sends data to those domains. See the External Services section below for full details.

storelens-insights-for-woocommerce.description:
Connect your WooCommerce store to an AI assistant and just ask:

  • “How did the store do this week compared to last week?”
  • “What do I need to reorder?”
  • “Which products made the most money this month?”
  • “Are any orders stuck?”

WooCommerce ships MCP tools for creating and editing products and orders. It does not ship a single reporting tool. This plugin fills that gap: seven read-only reports designed to be read by a language model, not by a human staring at a chart.

What your AI assistant gets

  • Sales summary — revenue, orders, average order value, refunds, and the percentage change against the previous period of equal length.
  • Sales trend — revenue bucketed by day, week or month, so the assistant can spot growth, decline and seasonality.
  • Top products — best sellers by revenue or by units, with SKU.
  • Low stock — what is running out, how fast it sells, and how many days of stock are left. This is the reorder question answered properly.
  • Customer insights — highest spending customers, repeat purchase rate, per-customer average order value.
  • Order status breakdown — orders and value per status, plus orders stuck in processing or on-hold for too long.
  • Store overview — the whole health check in a single call.

Built for people who are nervous about giving an AI access to their store

  • Read-only. Not one tool in this plugin can create, edit or delete anything. Ever.
  • No personal data. Customer reports return billing names only. Email addresses and postal addresses are never sent to the model.
  • Access log. Every request is recorded: which tool, which account, which arguments, how long it took. Visible in your dashboard.
  • Per-tool switches. Turn off any report you do not want exposed.
  • Standard WordPress permissions. Only users who can already view WooCommerce reports can run these tools.

Works with the official WordPress AI stack

Reports are registered through the WordPress Abilities API, which is part of WordPress core from 6.9. Install the official MCP Adapter plugin and this plugin publishes its own MCP endpoint, so Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and any other MCP client can connect directly. No local proxy process to babysit.

Without MCP Adapter the reports still work through the core Abilities REST API.

Accuracy notes

Revenue counts orders with status completed and processing. Refunds are reported separately and subtracted to give net revenue. All date handling uses your store timezone, not server time. Figures work on both High-Performance Order Storage and legacy post storage.

Pro

A paid tier adds four reports the free seven do not cover, plus two things that work while you are not looking:

  • Refund analysis — which products come back, what share of revenue leaves again, and the reasons staff recorded.
  • Coupon performance — order value earned for every unit of discount given, and whether coupon buyers spend more than everyone else.
  • Bought together — product pairs that share a basket more often than chance, with confidence read in both directions.
  • Customers going quiet — repeat buyers whose silence has run past twice their own usual gap between orders.
  • Digest by email — daily or Monday mornings, so a busy week does not become a blind week.
  • Alerts — a day compared against the same weekday rather than yesterday, orders left waiting, and products that just sold out.

Pro is a separate download, not a locked part of this plugin — this free version does not contain the Pro code at all. Buying a licence replaces this plugin with the Pro build. Pro is read-only too: nothing in either build can change your store. Details are on the WooCommerce → Storelens Insights Pro screen.

External services

Reports never leave your site. No order, product or customer data is sent anywhere by this plugin. The reports are handed to whichever AI client you connected, and that connection runs from your own server to your own client.

Freemius (licensing and payment). The Pro tier is sold and licensed through Freemius, a third-party service. The Freemius SDK is bundled with this plugin.

  • What it sends: your site URL, WordPress and PHP versions, plugin version, the site administrator’s name and email address, and the active plugin and theme list.
  • When: only after you explicitly opt in on the activation screen, and afterwards while a licence is active. If you skip the opt-in, the SDK stays quiet.
  • What it never sends: store data, orders, products, customers, revenue figures — none of it.
  • Service: Freemius · terms · privacy policy

Self-hosted licence server (optional). If you would rather not use Freemius, the mcpiw_license_verify_url filter points the licence check at a server you control. It then sends only the licence key, the site address and the plugin version.
storelens-insights-for-woocommerce.installation:
1. Install and activate this plugin.
  2. Install the official MCP Adapter plugin, if you want to connect an AI client directly.
  3. Go to WooCommerce → Storelens Insights and copy the endpoint address.
  4. Create an application password under Users → Profile. Do not use your login password.
  5. Add the endpoint and the application password to your AI client.
storelens-insights-for-woocommerce.faq:
Can the AI change anything in my store?

No. Every tool in this plugin only reads. If you want an AI to be able to edit products or orders, that is a separate feature shipped by WooCommerce itself, and you turn it on knowingly on the settings screen.

Does this send my customer data to an AI company?

Only what you ask for, and only the fields listed above. Customer reports contain billing names, order counts and totals. No email addresses, no phone numbers, no addresses. Whatever your AI client receives is governed by that client’s own privacy policy.

Does it slow down my store?

The reports run only when an AI asks for one. Nothing runs on page loads for your shoppers.

Do I need WooCommerce Analytics enabled?

No. The reports read orders directly, so they are correct even on stores where the analytics lookup tables were never populated.

Which WordPress version do I need?

WordPress 6.9 or newer, because that is when the Abilities API arrived in core.

open-for-agents-ai-toolkit-with-mcp.description:
Publish reviewed WordPress and WooCommerce capabilities as MCP and WebMCP tools. You choose what agents may discover, and supported changes require approval.

Install the plugin, enable Standard Tools, review the catalog, then publish and verify it. Core works without an Open for Agents account, AI API key or paid license, and nothing is published merely because the plugin was activated.

Open for Agents is for website owners who want agents to use reviewed site capabilities. It is not unrestricted WordPress administration.

What you can do

  • Publish reviewed public content, navigation, search, supported forms and WooCommerce capabilities.
  • Give compatible agents one owner-approved catalog instead of exposing arbitrary WordPress actions.
  • Verify the selected tools through the same public routes agents use.
  • Keep private, dangerous, unsupported and unapproved actions out of public exports.
  • Require trusted, argument-bound visitor approval before supported changes run.

Your first useful result

  1. Install and activate Open for Agents.
  2. Open Open for Agents > Setup and enable Standard Tools.
  3. Review the catalog and confirm what may be public.
  4. Choose Publish Safe Public and verify.
  5. Ask a currently verified compatible agent a tested question, such as requesting the site’s public information, and confirm the expected result.

Safe by default

Activation alone publishes nothing. Public publishing and the browser runtime are disabled by default, and detected forms or endpoints do not become tools automatically.

Safe Public includes only the reviewed public selection. An exact session-bound read such as cart inspection can be enabled without cart changes. Write tools still require the write framework and trusted, argument-bound visitor approval. Checkout, payment, order placement and account changes remain unavailable.

Core requires no Open for Agents account, model API key, paid license or hosted service. Every included capability remains available without a paid upgrade.

Supported content, forms and commerce

  • WordPress public site information, post types, navigation, posts, search, individual posts and terms.
  • WooCommerce 10.5.1 and 10.9.4: tested product discovery, session-bound cart inspection, visitor-approved reversible cart tools and declared HPOS compatibility.
  • Contact Form 7 6.1.5 and 6.1.6: tested detection, reviewed publication, and certified execution for supported single-page contact and choice fields.
  • WPForms Lite 1.9.9.2 and 1.10.2.1: tested detection, reviewed publication, and certified execution for supported single-page contact, number, choice, name and address fields.

Executable forms exclude captcha, consent, payment, upload, account, signature, calculation and multi-page workflows. Generic REST and AJAX mining is lower-confidence discovery for administrator review, not native provider support. Detection never means automatic publication; execution requires provider enablement, exact per-form opt-in and a trusted approval verifier.

Form preparation lets compatible browser assistants fill exact reviewed WPForms Lite and Contact Form 7 forms. Visitors check every answer and submit the form themselves.

How agents discover the catalog

MCP lets compatible external clients discover and call reviewed tools through a bounded server endpoint. WebMCP makes the same reviewed capabilities available to compatible browser agents on the relevant pages.

Core can also publish the owner-approved catalog through llms.txt, an API Catalog, an MCP Server Card, Agent Skills and optional Agentic Resource Discovery output. AI crawler controls for robots.txt, validation, diagnostics and scan history help administrators understand the published surface.

Optional Assistant

The separately distributed Open for Agents Assistant is optional and is not included in this WordPress.org package. It is available only for approved deployments, not general public download. Core works without it.

Documentation and demonstration

  • Getting started guide
  • Documentation
  • Live WordPress demonstration
  • Open for Agents website

External services

Core does not contact an external service operated by Enoki Limited or another provider.

Published MCP Server Card and Agent Skills documents contain $schema identifiers at static.modelcontextprotocol.io and schemas.agentskills.io. The plugin does not request those URLs, transmit data to them or require them to be available.

Deep scan is an optional developer integration point, not a bundled service. When enabled, the plugin passes a page URL and non-secret request settings only to locally installed code attached to open_for_agents_deep_scan_report; it never passes authentication cookies, authorization headers or WordPress nonces. A developer who connects an external renderer must disclose that separate service, its data, terms and privacy policy. Without an integration, the plugin uses its same-site static scan and sends nothing externally.

Privacy

Core does not create an Enoki Limited account, load remote tracking code or transmit site data to an Open for Agents service.

Normal scanning and verification make HTTP requests to the WordPress site’s own public or administrator-authorized same-origin URLs. Authenticated scan cookies are used only for same-origin requests during that scan and are never included in public output.

Any configured third-party renderer may process page URLs, request context or rendered content and must be governed separately.

Privacy policy: Open for Agents privacy policy

Terms: Open for Agents terms
open-for-agents-ai-toolkit-with-mcp.installation:
1. Install and activate Open for Agents.
  2. Open Open for Agents > Setup and enable Standard Tools.
  3. Optionally scan for supported site-specific workflows.
  4. Review the catalog, visibility, risk and execution policy.
  5. Choose Publish Safe Public and verify to check, publish and verify the selected public tools.

Upgrading preserves existing settings, reviewed actions, scan history and publication state.
open-for-agents-ai-toolkit-with-mcp.faq:
Does activation immediately expose my site to agents?

No. Public publishing and the browser runtime are disabled by default. An administrator must review and enable them.

Does the plugin send my content or credentials to Open for Agents?

No. Core sends no site content, credentials, scan results or visitor data to Enoki Limited or Open for Agents. A separately configured deep-scan renderer controls its own data handling.

Do I need an AI API key?

No. Scanning, review, validation, publication, discovery endpoints, MCP and WebMCP runtime support do not require a model API key.

Which integrations are supported?

The scanner supports WordPress core, WooCommerce core, Contact Form 7 and WPForms Lite. Selected custom REST and AJAX surfaces appear as lower-confidence review candidates.

Can an agent place an order or make a payment?

No. Checkout, payment, order placement and account changes are excluded. Cart inspection is an exact opt-in session read. Cart changes remain disabled by default and require trusted, argument-bound visitor approval.

What is published?

Only the administrator-approved public catalog and enabled discovery formats. Private scan evidence, cookies, credentials, nonces, logs and admin-only data are not published.

site-answers-llms-txt-ai-crawler-log-mar.description:
AI assistants are reading your website. Site Answers has one job: make your site
readable to them, show you whether they actually came, let you decide which of them
may, and let the AI agents you choose search and read it directly. These parts make a
WordPress site agent-ready, and together they are the whole plugin.

It is a read-only MCP server for AI agents. MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is the
standard way AI assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor connect to tools. Make a token
under Site Answers → AI Agents (MCP), give your agent the address and the token, and it can
search your published posts and pages and read any of them as clean Markdown. It gets four
tools: search_content, get_post, list_recent and get_site_info. It cannot change
anything: there are no write tools at all, not even switched-off ones. Each token is
revocable and limited to 60 calls a minute, and the access log shows which token used which
tool on which page, and when. If your site runs WordPress’s official MCP Adapter plugin, the
same four tools are registered as WordPress abilities too, so its agents get them with no
token at all.

It publishes an llms.txt file. llms.txt is an emerging convention — a plain,
readable Markdown index at the root of your site that tells AI assistants what you
have published and where to find it. Site Answers builds yours from your own posts and
pages: your site name, your tagline, then one line per URL with its title and a short
description. It is rebuilt automatically whenever you publish, edit or delete
something, so it never goes stale.

It publishes llms-full.txt too. Where llms.txt is the map, llms-full.txt is the
whole territory: the full text of every page llms.txt lists, one after another, in one file,
so an AI assistant can read your site in a single visit. Same pages, same exclusions, capped at
5 MB with a note saying where the rest is. You can switch it off in Settings.

It logs which AI crawlers visit. GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, OAI-SearchBot,
CCBot and the others are recognised by name. For each visit you see which crawler
came, which page it asked for, and whether it got the page or an error. That answers a
question site owners currently cannot answer at all: is AI search actually reading my
content, and which pages does it want?

It serves a clean Markdown copy of every page. Add .md to the end of any post or page
address and you get the article as plain Markdown — headings, paragraphs, lists, links and
tables — with the navigation, sidebars, share buttons and scripts left out. That is what an
automated reader wants, and it is far less likely to be misquoted than a page it had to dig out
of a theme. Each HTML page also advertises its Markdown twin in a Link header, so a crawler
can find it without guessing.

It tells you when your robots.txt is turning AI crawlers away. An empty crawler log often
has a simple cause: a line in robots.txt — added by another plugin, a host, or years ago by
hand — asking GPTBot or ClaudeBot to stay away. The Overview reads the robots.txt your site
actually serves, the way the crawlers read it, and names every AI crawler it blocks.

And it lets you choose, crawler by crawler. In Settings, each AI crawler has three
choices: No change, Allow or Block. Block ChatGPT’s training crawler and keep the one that
fetches your page when someone asks ChatGPT about you, or the other way round. Your choices go
into WordPress’s own robots.txt. Until you pick something, robots.txt stays exactly as it was.

How this is different

Plenty of plugins will write an llms.txt for you. Almost all of them stop at that point: the
file is written, and you never find out whether anything read it. This one closes the loop — it
publishes the file, serves your pages in a form a machine can actually read, and then shows you
whether any AI crawler turned up and what it asked for. Publishing without measuring is
guesswork, and until now measuring meant reading raw server logs.

The same goes for MCP. Many MCP plugins hand an agent your whole WordPress through an
application password, which can do anything that user can, writing included. This one is
read-only by construction, its tokens can do exactly one thing and are revoked in one click,
and every tool returns the same clean Markdown text the .md addresses serve, not raw page
HTML for the agent to dig through.

Three further differences, each of which you can check in the code:

  • It stands aside rather than fighting for the address. If another plugin, or a static file
    in your web root, already serves /llms.txt, Site Answers never registers its own route for it:
    theirs keeps working untouched, and your settings screen tells you which one is answering. Two
    plugins answering one address is how sites break, and it is always the newer plugin that gets
    blamed for it.
  • It keeps nothing personal. The crawler log holds the crawler’s name, the page path, the
    response status and the time. No IP addresses, no query strings, no headers — so it never grows
    into a consent-banner problem the way a general-purpose visitor log does.
  • It asks for nothing. No account, no API key, no external service, no outbound request of
    any kind, and nothing to upgrade to. Everything happens on your own server, so nothing about
    your site or your visitors leaves it.

What it does not do

This plugin does not connect to any external service. It makes no outbound HTTP request
of any kind — no API, no phone-home, no telemetry, no analytics, no third-party
libraries. Everything it shows you was produced by your own site, on your own server.
AI agents you connect over MCP send requests to your site; your site never contacts them.

It stores no IP addresses. The crawler log records the crawler’s name, the page path and
the time — nothing else. The MCP access log records the token (or the WordPress user), the
tool, the page read or the words searched, and the time. Anything after the ? in an address is discarded before the
record is written, because query strings on real sites carry e-mail addresses, order
references and reset tokens. Records older than 90 days are deleted automatically.

It changes nothing on its own. Your robots.txt is left exactly as it is until you choose
Allow or Block for a crawler, and no file is ever written to your server: if you have a
robots.txt file of your own, the plugin tells you so and leaves it alone.

Why this matters

AI assistants increasingly answer questions using content they read from websites, and being
readable to them is becoming its own discipline — answer engine optimization, or AEO, alongside
the generative engine optimization people now talk about next to ordinary SEO. Both come down
to the same two practical questions: can a large language model find and parse what you
published, and is it actually doing so? Site Answers gives you a straight answer to the second
one, and does the groundwork for the first.

Who it is for

Anyone who publishes writing and wants to know whether AI search engines are reading it.
Bloggers, documentation sites, shops with real content, agencies who need to show a
client what is happening.

Privacy

No personal data of any kind is collected, stored or transmitted. Because no IP address
is recorded and nothing leaves your server, this plugin does not put your site into
consent-banner territory.
site-answers-llms-txt-ai-crawler-log-mar.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Visit Site Answers → Overview. Your llms.txt link is at the top.
  3. Optionally visit Site Answers → Settings to choose which content is listed and which AI crawlers may read your site.
  4. To let an AI agent read your site over MCP, visit Site Answers → AI Agents (MCP), make a token, and paste the address and the token into your agent. The screen shows a ready-made command and configuration to copy.

There is nothing to sign up for. The MCP tokens are made on your own site and never leave it unless you give one to an agent.
site-answers-llms-txt-ai-crawler-log-mar.faq:
What is llms.txt?

It is a proposed convention — like robots.txt or sitemap.xml, but written for large
language models. A single Markdown file at /llms.txt that tells an AI assistant what a
site contains, in a form it can read without wading through navigation, adverts and
scripts. It is young and not every AI engine reads it yet, which is exactly why it costs
almost nothing to publish one now.

Where is my llms.txt?

At /llms.txt on your site, and the Overview screen links straight to it.

What is llms-full.txt?

The companion to llms.txt. Instead of a list of links, it holds the full text of every page
llms.txt lists, as Markdown, in one file at /llms-full.txt. Each page starts with its title
and a Source: line with its address. It leaves out exactly what llms.txt leaves out —
drafts, private and password-protected posts, and pages marked “noindex” — and stops at 5 MB.
On a large site the first visit may not include every page yet: pages are converted a few at a
time so the file never times out, and the file says so when that happens.

My llms.txt says “not found”. Why?

Almost always because Settings → Reading → “Discourage search engines from indexing
this site” is switched on. Site Answers honours that: if you have asked search engines
to stay away, it does not publish an index of your content on your behalf. The Overview
screen tells you when this is the reason. Switch that setting off and the file appears
immediately.

If that setting is already off, something else is probably answering at that address: a
static llms.txt file in your site’s root folder, or another plugin that publishes one.
Site Answers steps aside for both rather than fight over the address, and the Overview
screen names whichever it is.

Which AI crawlers are detected?

GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot and ChatGPT-User (OpenAI); ClaudeBot, Claude-User and anthropic-ai
(Anthropic); PerplexityBot and Perplexity-User (Perplexity); Google-Extended and
GoogleOther (Google); CCBot (Common Crawl); Bytespider (ByteDance); Amazonbot (Amazon);
Applebot-Extended (Apple); Meta-ExternalAgent (Meta); cohere-ai (Cohere); DuckAssistBot
(DuckDuckGo); YouBot (You.com); and Diffbot.

Google-Extended and Applebot-Extended are robots.txt names only: Google and Apple fetch pages
with their ordinary crawlers and use these names to let you opt out of AI training. They can
be blocked in Settings, but they never appear in the visit log.

How do I get the Markdown version of a page?

Add .md to the end of its address. A post at https://example.com/hello-world/ is also
served at https://example.com/hello-world.md. The HTML page carries a
Link: <…>; rel=”alternate”; type=”text/markdown” header pointing at it, which is how an
automated reader is meant to discover it.

Drafts, private posts, password-protected posts and anything you have marked “noindex”
are not served this way, exactly as they are kept out of llms.txt. The Markdown copy
also carries X-Robots-Tag: noindex and a canonical link back to the real page, so it
cannot compete with your own article in search results.

What is MCP, and how do I connect an AI agent to my site?

MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is the open standard AI assistants use to connect to tools
and data. Site Answers turns your site into a read-only MCP server:

  1. Go to Site Answers → AI Agents (MCP) and make a token. Give it a name you will
    recognise, such as “Claude on my laptop”.
  2. Copy the token straight away: it is shown once, and only a fingerprint of it is kept.
  3. Give your agent the MCP server address shown on that screen (it ends in
    /wp-json/site-answers/v1/mcp) and send the token as Authorization: Bearer <token>. The
    screen has a ready-made Claude Code command and a JSON block for clients such as Cursor and
    VS Code that take an address and headers.

The agent then has four tools: search_content (search your posts and pages),
get_post (read one in full, as Markdown, by id or address), list_recent (the newest
content) and get_site_info (your site’s name, language, content types and llms.txt
address).

Can an AI agent change my site through MCP?

No. There are no write tools: the code to create, edit or delete anything does not exist
in this plugin, so there is nothing a token, a bug or a setting could switch on. A token can
read what your llms.txt lists and nothing else, and revoking it stops it on its very next
call.

Which content can an agent read?

Exactly what llms.txt lists: the content types ticked in Settings, published, with no
password, and nothing marked “noindex” by your SEO plugin. Drafts, private posts and
password-protected posts are never reachable, even through an administrator’s agent. The
siteanswers_mcp_exclude_post filter withholds any other post in code. The “Discourage
search engines” setting does not close the MCP server, because a token is you personally
giving your own agent a key.

Does it work with the WordPress MCP Adapter?

Yes. On WordPress 6.9 and newer the four tools are also registered with WordPress’s
Abilities API as site-answers/search-content, site-answers/get-post,
site-answers/list-recent and site-answers/get-site-info. If you use the official MCP
Adapter plugin, its agents find them with no further setup, signed in as a WordPress user
rather than with a Site Answers token, and their calls appear in the same access log. You
can switch this off in Settings.

My agent gets “401” or “unauthorized”. What now?

Check that the token is sent as Authorization: Bearer <token> and has not been revoked.
If it is right and still refused, your host may be dropping the Authorization header before
WordPress sees it. This happens on some Apache servers, and adding
SetEnvIf Authorization “(.*)” HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=$1 to your .htaccess fixes it. A security
plugin that blocks the WordPress REST API for logged-out visitors will also block the MCP
address; allow site-answers/v1 in its settings.

Is there a limit on how much an agent can read?

Each token may make 60 tool calls a minute, which is plenty for an agent researching your
site and stops a runaway one from loading your server. A page longer than 100 KB of text is
cut there, and the agent is told so.

Does this plugin send anything to anyone?

No. It makes no outbound HTTP request at all. There is no account, no API key, no
telemetry and no analytics of any kind. AI agents you connect over MCP send requests to your
site; your site never contacts them.

The Overview and AI Agents (MCP) screens carry one ordinary link, “Get early access”, to a
page about a possible paid add-on. Nothing is sent when a screen loads; the page opens in your
browser only if you click, and your e-mail address reaches us only if you type it there.

Is there a paid version?

Not yet. Everything described here is free and stays free. We are considering an optional
paid add-on that answers your visitors’ questions from your own content; the “Get early
access” link on the Overview and AI Agents (MCP) screens lets you ask to be told if it is built. It is never
shown as a notice, and nothing in this plugin is locked behind it.

Does it record IP addresses?

No. The crawler name, the page path and the time — that is the whole record. Query
strings are discarded too. The MCP access log stores no IP address either: only the token
or WordPress user, the tool, the page read or the words searched, and the time.

My server log shows more AI crawler visits than this plugin does. Why?

If your site uses full-page caching — nginx FastCGI cache, WP Rocket, Cloudflare, a host
level cache — then a cached page is served without WordPress running at all, so the
plugin never sees that visit. This is true of every WordPress-level bot log, not just
this one. Treat the numbers here as a floor rather than a total.

Does it work with my SEO plugin?

Yes. If a page is marked “noindex” in Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress or The SEO
Framework, Site Answers leaves it out of llms.txt by default. You can turn that off in
Settings. For any other rule, the siteanswers_llms_txt_exclude_post filter lets you
exclude a page in code.

Will it list my drafts or private posts?

No. Only published content. Drafts, pending, private, trashed and password-protected
posts are never listed, whatever you choose in Settings.

What happens when I delete the plugin?

Everything it created is removed: both of its database tables (the crawler log and the MCP
access log), its MCP tokens, every option and cached value it wrote, and its scheduled
cleanup job. Deactivating the plugin, by contrast, leaves your
crawler history intact so you can switch it back on without losing anything.

Can I block AI crawlers like GPTBot?

Yes, if you choose to. Site Answers → Settings has a choice for every crawler it knows:
No change, Allow or Block. Block adds a Disallow: / rule for that crawler to your
robots.txt; Allow adds a rule inviting it in. Nothing changes until you choose, and each
crawler’s row says what it is for — some collect training data, others open your page only
when someone asks an AI assistant about it, and blocking those means the assistant cannot read
you when asked.

robots.txt is a request that well-behaved crawlers follow, not a lock. If your site has a
robots.txt file of its own on the server, WordPress’s robots.txt is never used, so the choices
cannot apply — the Settings screen tells you when that is the case.

Why does the Overview say my robots.txt blocks a crawler I never blocked?

Because something else did: another plugin, your host, or a line in a robots.txt file on your
server. The Overview reads the robots.txt your visitors actually get and names every AI
crawler it turns away, whoever wrote the rule. If you set a crawler to Allow and another rule
still blocks it, the Overview says that too.

windcodex-forge.description:
WindCodex Forge gives Claude, ChatGPT, and other MCP-compatible AI assistants a small number of general-purpose, read-only tools for understanding a WordPress site: installed plugins, active theme, registered hooks, files within wp-content, database structure and data (read-only), Gutenberg content blocks, and cross-conversation memory.

This plugin is entirely free and read-only – it inspects a site’s plugins, theme, hooks, files, and database, but cannot change any of them. The only data it ever writes is its own: memory notes and an activity log.

Why Developers Choose WindCodex Forge

  • Safe to run on a live site – no tool can change your content, settings, users, plugins, theme, files, or database tables.
  • No code-execution capability at all – that’s not a setting to be careful with; it simply isn’t present in the codebase.
  • Administrators stay in control – only Administrators can connect an AI app by default, every tool call is logged, and login credentials are never returned.
  • Real diagnostics, not guesswork – let an AI read hook registrations, database schema, and file contents directly instead of asking you to paste them in.
  • Cross-conversation memory – save a fact or preference once so a future, separate conversation can pick it back up.
  • No license key, no paywall – every tool in this plugin is free.

Key Features

18 tools across 4 groups, entirely free, no license key required:

  • Site introspection – installed plugins, active theme, registered hooks, screenshots, static page inspection, recent connector activity, and design-authority detection (works out whether an active page builder or the theme’s own design tokens should govern new visual work).
  • File read – browse and read file contents within wp-content (themes, plugins, uploads).
  • Database read – read rows from any table using structured filters (columns, conditions, sorting, paging) that always run as prepared statements – no raw SQL is accepted – plus table listing and schema introspection. Password hashes, reset keys, session tokens, application passwords, and secret-looking option/meta values are never returned.
  • Content blocks (read-only) – read a Gutenberg block’s full structure (attributes, inner HTML) by position, and list registered reusable blocks.
  • Memory – wp_remember/wp_list_memories/wp_forget let a conversation save a fact or preference site-wide so a future, separate conversation can pick it back up. Plaintext, not a secrets vault; capped at 200 entries per site.

Plus, in the plugin’s settings:

  • Access control – choose who may approve an AI connection (Administrators only by default, or Editors and above). Each connection is limited to that person’s own permissions and stops working as soon as they lose the role.
  • Activity log – every tool call, successful or not, is recorded with its arguments, the user whose connection made it, and when.
  • Per-tool switches – turn any individual tool off.

A flat 120 requests/minute rate limit applies.

Use Cases

  • Ask an AI to explain why a page looks the way it does by reading the active theme, registered hooks, and page builder in use.
  • Debug a data issue by reading rows from your live database without ever risking a write.
  • Have an AI review a plugin’s or theme’s source files directly from wp-content before suggesting a fix.
  • Take a screenshot of a page and inspect its structure as part of a support or QA workflow.
  • Let a future conversation pick up context – naming conventions, prior decisions, site quirks – saved by an earlier one via memory.
  • Audit which connectors and AI platforms have accessed the site recently.

For Developers

Every tool here is read-only, so this plugin is built for understanding a client site or codebase quickly, not editing it live:

  • Onboard onto an unfamiliar client site fast – ask an AI to list active plugins and theme, then read the hooks a specific feature actually depends on, instead of grepping through an unfamiliar codebase by hand.
  • Track down a plugin conflict by reading exactly what’s hooked into a given action or filter, across every active plugin, before touching any code.
  • Review a plugin’s or theme’s source file straight from wp-content as part of a code review or before writing a patch, without needing FTP/SSH access to the server.
  • Read rows from the live database with simple filters to confirm a bug’s root cause (bad meta value, orphaned row, wrong option) before writing the fix.
  • Take a screenshot of a broken page and get a structural read on it – markup, blocks, active builder – to speed up a bug report or a QA handoff.
  • Save project-specific conventions to memory once (naming patterns, past architectural decisions, known quirks of the client’s stack) so the next debugging session with the same site doesn’t start from zero.

Why This Is Safe on a Live Site

This plugin has no code-execution capability and no tool that can change your site – that’s not a setting to be careful with, it simply isn’t present in the codebase. The memory tools write only to the plugin’s own notes table.

On top of that:

  • Only approved people can connect. Administrators only by default. Each connection is limited to the permissions of the person who approved it – there is no shared or fallback account – and stops working immediately if they lose that role. The connection never logs in as that person; it can only read.
  • No access to your internal network. The page-inspection tool only fetches public web addresses and the site’s own pages, never private or local network addresses.
  • Sensitive tools need an Administrator. File and database tools always require an Administrator account, whatever the connection setting.
  • Credentials stay private. The database tool refuses requests that select, filter, or sort on password hashes, reset keys, session tokens, or application passwords, and redacts secret-looking values.
  • Everything is logged and revocable. Every call appears on the Activity tab, and any connected app can be revoked from the Connection tab.

How It Works

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Go to Settings > WindCodex Forge and copy the Connector URL from the Connection tab.
  3. Add it to Claude, ChatGPT, or any other MCP-compatible AI platform as a custom connector.
  4. Authenticate once via OAuth while logged in as an Administrator – most platforms register themselves automatically from the discovery URLs on the Connection tab.
  5. The AI can now read plugins, files, the database, and content blocks – but never change them.

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.2 or higher
  • PHP 7.4 or higher
  • An MCP-compatible AI platform (Claude, ChatGPT, or similar) to connect to
  • No account or API key required. The optional screenshot tool asks a public WordPress.com screenshot service to render a page, so that page’s URL is sent to it (you can switch that tool off in Settings > WindCodex Forge > Tools)

Privacy

This plugin has no code-execution capability and no tool that can change your site. Every tool call is recorded in an activity log stored in your own database. Memory storage is plaintext, not encrypted – not meant for secrets or credentials. All tool calls run locally against your own site through WordPress’s normal APIs, and the plugin talks only to the AI platform you connect over the OAuth connector you set up yourself. The one exception is the optional screenshot tool, which sends the requested page’s URL to a public WordPress.com screenshot service; switch it off on the Tools tab if that isn’t acceptable. By default, deleting the plugin leaves all data in place; opt into full cleanup via Settings > WindCodex Forge > General > Data & Privacy.

External services

This plugin connects to the following external services:

The AI platform you connect (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, or any other MCP-compatible client)

The entire purpose of this plugin is to let an AI platform you choose to connect – over the OAuth connector you set up yourself in Settings > WindCodex Forge > Connection – read a fixed list of diagnostic information from your site. When that platform calls an enabled tool, this plugin sends back only what that specific tool returns (for example: plugin/theme/hook listings, file contents from wp-content, database query results, or Gutenberg block structure), and only in direct response to that tool call. Nothing is sent proactively, on a schedule, or to any platform you haven’t explicitly connected and authorized via OAuth. Because you choose which platform to connect, its terms and privacy policy are the platform’s own – for example, Anthropic’s (https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms and https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy) or OpenAI’s (https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use and https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy).

WordPress.com mshots screenshot service (s.wordpress.com)

The “Take Screenshot” tool (wp_take_screenshot), when called by your connected AI, asks WordPress.com’s free, public mshots service to render a screenshot of a URL – the URL is sent to https://s.wordpress.com/mshots/v1/ as part of the request, and the target page must be publicly reachable for a screenshot to render. This only happens when that specific tool is invoked, and it can be turned off entirely in Settings > WindCodex Forge > Tools. This service is operated by Automattic; see its terms (https://wordpress.com/tos/) and privacy policy (https://automattic.com/privacy/).
windcodex-forge.installation:
From your WordPress dashboard

  1. Go to Plugins > Add New.
  2. Search for WindCodex Forge.
  3. Click Install Now, then Activate.

Manual installation

  1. Download the plugin ZIP file.
  2. Upload the windcodex-forge folder to /wp-content/plugins/.

windcodex-forge.faq:
Is it safe to run this on my live, production site?

Yes. This plugin has no code-execution capability and no tool that can change your site’s content, settings, users, plugins, theme, files, or database tables.

Can the AI modify my database or files with this plugin?

No. This plugin only exposes read-only tools – database reads, file reads, and read-only content-block inspection. There is no write or code-execution capability anywhere in the codebase. The one exception is the memory tools, which save and delete notes in the plugin’s own table.

How does authentication work?

OAuth only. Most platforms register themselves automatically via the discovery URLs shown on the Connection tab. If auto-registration fails, paste the Client ID/Secret from that same tab into the platform’s Advanced/OAuth settings instead. The Connection tab lists every app that’s ever connected, who it’s currently acting as, and lets you revoke any one of them individually.

Who can connect an AI app?

Only Administrators, by default. Anyone else who reaches the consent screen is told their account isn’t allowed to connect. To let Editors connect too, change Settings > WindCodex Forge > General > Who can connect. Even then, the file and database tools still require an Administrator.

Does this plugin phone home or require an account?

No. There’s no license key and no account, and nothing is sent to WindCodex. It talks to the AI platform you connect, over the OAuth connector you set up yourself. The one exception is the screenshot tool (wp_take_screenshot), which asks a public WordPress.com screenshot service to render a page, so that page’s URL is sent to that service and the page must be publicly reachable. You can switch that tool off on the Tools tab.

What can the database read tool actually see?

Rows from any table in your WordPress database, plus schema introspection (table listing and column structure). The AI never sends SQL: it names a table, the columns it wants, and simple conditions (e.g. option_name LIKE 'woocommerce_%'), and the plugin builds the query itself – table and column names are checked against your actual schema, and every value is passed through $wpdb->prepare(). It can only ever produce a single SELECT on one table, so it cannot change data, read files, or write to disk.

Login credentials are never returned: requests that name password hashes, password-reset keys, session tokens, or application passwords are refused, and any value that looks like a password hash – or an option/meta value whose name looks like a password, secret, API key, or token – is replaced with [redacted].

Whose permissions does the AI use?

Those of the WordPress user who logged in and approved the connection on the consent screen – there is no shared or fallback account. If that user later loses the role allowed to connect, or is deleted, the connection stops working immediately. Every tool call is recorded on the Activity tab with its arguments and whether it succeeded, and you can revoke any connected app from the Connection tab at any time.

What is the memory feature for?

wp_remember, wp_list_memories, and wp_forget let one AI conversation save a fact or preference about the site so a completely separate, future conversation can pick it up automatically – useful for naming conventions, past decisions, or site-specific quirks. It’s plaintext and capped at 200 entries per site, not intended for secrets.

Which AI platforms can connect to WindCodex Forge?

Any platform that supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as a client, including Claude and ChatGPT. Connection uses standard OAuth, so most platforms auto-register themselves from the discovery URLs on the Connection tab.

Can I see which files the AI has access to?

The File read tool is scoped to wp-content (themes, plugins, uploads) only – it cannot read files outside of that directory, such as wp-config.php or core WordPress files.

elementor.installation:
Minimum Requirements

  • WordPress 6.8 or greater
  • PHP version 7.4 or greater
  • MySQL version 5.6 or MariaDB version 10.5 or greater
  • PHP Memory limit of 256 MB or greater
  • WordPress Memory limit of 256 MB or greater

Recommended Requirements

  • WordPress 7.0 or greater
  • PHP version 8.3 or greater
  • MySQL version 8.0 or MariaDB version 10.6 or greater
  • PHP Memory limit of 512 MB (768 MB for best performance) or greater
  • WordPress Memory limit of 512 MB (768 MB for best performance) or greater

Note: These requirements are for Elementor and Elementor Pro only. If you are using additional plugins on your site that also have minimum requirements such as WooCommerce or Elementor addons, you may need to increase your PHP and WordPress Memory limit to help avoid loading issues. See also, the following documentation Elementor Widget Panel Not Loading.

Installation

  1. Install using the WordPress built-in Plugin installer, or Extract the zip file and drop the contents in the wp-content/plugins/ directory of your WordPress installation.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Go to Pages > Add New
  4. Press the ‘Edit with Elementor’ button.
  5. Now you can drag and drop widgets from the left panel onto the content area, as well as add new sections and columns that make up the page structure.

For documentation and tutorials visit our Knowledge Base.
elementor.faq:
How do I install Elementor?

To install the free version of Elementor, follow the steps below:
From your WordPress dashboard -> Go to Plugins -> Click on ‘Add new’-> In the Search field, enter Elementor and choose Elementor website builder.
Press install -> After installation, click Activate.

Does Elementor work with all the themes?

Elementor works with any theme that respects the coding standards of WordPress set by its Codex. We recommend using Elementor’s Hello Theme, a lightweight blank canvas, to enjoy full flexibility when using Elementor Editor, and optimize your experience.

Is Elementor compatible with Gutenberg?

Elementor and Gutenberg work together. You can easily decide which editor to use at every point while editing your site.

Can I create an online store?

Yes, with the Elementor Pro WooCommerce Builder you can customize every page of your store to build a customer experience that drives sales.

Does it work with other WordPress plugins?

It works with almost all the plugins. If you experience an incompatibility issue, please report it to us and to the plugin that conflicts with Elementor.

Do I need to know how to code?

No. Elementor provides you with all the widgets and features that you need to build a professional website without using code.

Do I need to know how to design?

No. Choose between professionally designed kits and templates that fit to every industry and have all you need to create your own professional website.

Will Elementor slow down my website?

As Elementor prioritizes speed and performance, you enjoy better and faster performance with each new version of the Editor. When testing the same page layout on older versions you can see a significant performance improvement, from a score of 82 in Google PageSpeed Insight in version 3.1, to a score of 95 in version 3.5.

Is my site secure with Elementor?

The security of your website matters to us and we take proactive measures to keep your websites secure. Elementor is ISO 27001 certified, and has a dedicated team of security professionals that implements industry best-practices for maximum security and compliance, 24/7.

There is also a managed security Bug Bounty program, using the power of community for 24/7/365 crowdsourced vulnerability detection.

Can I buy templates separately?

Yes. you can use any template that supports Elementor

Is Elementor compatible with Post and Custom Post Types?

Yes. You can set which post types will enable Elementor in the settings page.

What is the difference between Elementor’s free Editor plugin and Elementor Pro?

Elementor’s Free version gives you our drag & drop live editor, basic widgets and templates. Elementor Pro (Essential, Advanced, Expert, Studio, and Agency) adds professional tools that speed up your workflow, help you build more advanced content, and convert visitors.

How can I become a Contributor?

If you want to contribute, go to our Elementor GitHub Repository and see where you can help. You can also add a new language via translate.wordpress.org. We’ve built a short guide explaining how to translate and localize the plugin.

premium-addons-for-elementor.installation:
1. Install and activate the free Elementor plugin. Premium Addons works only with Elementor.
  2. Upload the plugin to /wp-content/plugins/ or install it from the WordPress Plugins screen, then activate it.
  3. Find the widgets under the “Premium Addons” category in the Elementor editor panel, and the templates library button on any container.
