  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen.
  3. Open VX in the admin menu and create your first fieldset.
vx-framework.faq:
Does it work with the block editor?

Yes. Field values are available as dynamic data inside the block
editor. You can bind them to blocks, loop them, and drive visibility
from the same model.

Can an AI assistant work with my model?

Yes. VX registers its operations as WordPress abilities and can serve
them over MCP. The endpoint stays off until you enable it.

Can I define the model in code?

Yes. Register fieldsets, post types, and taxonomies in PHP or JSON
in your theme or plugin. The dashboard stays usable for everything
that is not in code.

Does it work with Bricks Builder?

Yes. When Bricks Builder is active, VX fields appear in its dynamic data
picker.

draftfence-ai-review.description:
DraftFence AI Review is a governance layer for AI agents connected to WordPress. It gives authenticated AI identities a narrow, reviewable set of capabilities: list allowed content summaries, create draft-only content, and submit content or SEO changes as proposals for human review.

DraftFence AI Review is designed for site owners, agencies, SEO teams, and editorial teams who want AI help without handing an assistant unrestricted publishing power.

Key Features

  • Emergency switch to disable DraftFence AI Review AI operations immediately.
  • First-run onboarding wizard for guided setup.
  • Draft-only content creation for posts, pages, and selected REST-enabled public post types.
  • Human approval workflow for edits to existing content.
  • Before/after proposal review for titles, excerpts, and SEO fields.
  • Full content comparison using the snapshot captured when the proposal was created.
  • Risk badges that flag larger or more sensitive proposed changes.
  • AI identity profiles for per-user action, post type, risk, and payload limits.
  • Separate AI and human reviewer capabilities.
  • Conflict detection that blocks approval when content changed after proposal creation.
  • One-click rollback for approved proposals.
  • Email notifications for pending proposal review.
  • SEO title and description support for Yoast SEO, Rank Math, and AIOSEO-style meta keys.
  • Per-user hourly rate limits for AI operations.
  • Audit logs for allowed, blocked, failed, approved, and rejected actions.
  • Filterable audit screen with CSV export.
  • Configurable audit retention with daily pruning.
  • WordPress Abilities API registration when available.
  • REST API endpoints under /wp-json/draftfence-ai-review/v1/.

Why DraftFence AI Review?

Many WordPress AI plugins focus on generating content or exposing a broad MCP bridge. DraftFence AI Review focuses on governance: clear boundaries, human approval, operational limits, and reviewable logs. It can sit beside your preferred AI client, MCP adapter, or SEO plugin as the policy layer for content and SEO changes.

REST Endpoints

All endpoints require an authenticated WordPress user with the right capability. Application Passwords are recommended for AI client identities.

  • GET /wp-json/draftfence-ai-review/v1/status
  • GET /wp-json/draftfence-ai-review/v1/content?post_type=post&limit=20
  • POST /wp-json/draftfence-ai-review/v1/drafts
  • GET /wp-json/draftfence-ai-review/v1/proposals
  • POST /wp-json/draftfence-ai-review/v1/proposals
  • POST /wp-json/draftfence-ai-review/v1/proposals/{id}/approve
  • POST /wp-json/draftfence-ai-review/v1/proposals/{id}/reject
  • POST /wp-json/draftfence-ai-review/v1/proposals/{id}/rollback

WordPress Abilities

When the WordPress Abilities API is available, DraftFence AI Review registers:

  • draftfence-ai-review/status
  • draftfence-ai-review/list-content
  • draftfence-ai-review/create-draft
  • draftfence-ai-review/propose-content-seo-update
  • draftfence-ai-review/list-pending-proposals
  • draftfence-ai-review/approve-proposal
  • draftfence-ai-review/reject-proposal
  • draftfence-ai-review/rollback-approved-proposal
draftfence-ai-review.installation:
1. Upload the draftfence-ai-review folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate DraftFence AI Review from the WordPress Plugins screen.
  3. Open DraftFence AI Review > Settings.
  4. Choose allowed post types, rate limits, retention, and permitted AI actions.
  5. Create a dedicated WordPress user for your AI client and authenticate with an Application Password.
  6. Open DraftFence AI Review > AI Identities and assign that user an DraftFence AI Review profile.
  7. Or use DraftFence AI Review > Onboarding to complete the guided first-run setup.
draftfence-ai-review.faq:
Does DraftFence AI Review publish AI-generated content?

No. DraftFence AI Review creates new content as drafts. Existing content changes are stored as pending proposals until an administrator approves them.

Can an AI approve its own changes?

No. DraftFence AI Review separates AI identities from reviewer accounts. An AI identity can request work, but a different reviewer account must approve it.

Can I roll back an approved AI change?

Yes. DraftFence AI Review stores the original content and SEO values with each proposal and can restore them from the proposal review screen.

Does DraftFence AI Review require an external AI service?

No. DraftFence AI Review does not call an external AI provider. It controls what authenticated AI clients are allowed to do inside WordPress.

Which SEO plugins are supported?

DraftFence AI Review writes SEO title and description values to common Yoast SEO, Rank Math, and AIOSEO meta keys.

Can I turn off AI access quickly?

Yes. The emergency switch blocks DraftFence AI Review REST and Ability operations while leaving the admin review screens available to administrators.

Does DraftFence AI Review replace a full activity log plugin?

No. DraftFence AI Review logs its own AI-related operations. For full-site activity monitoring, use a dedicated activity log plugin alongside DraftFence AI Review.

belayline-agent-governance.description:
Belayline Agent Governance governs other plugins’ agent tool calls, not just its own. It sits between AI
agents (through the WordPress Abilities API, and through MCP servers built on
mcp-adapter, as WooCommerce’s is) and the actions
those agents can take on your site. Every governed call is classified by tier, checked against a
capability pack bound to the calling identity, and written to a tamper-evident, hash-chained
audit log, before it runs.

The plugin is WordPress-general. It ships a core/* module that runs on every site, and a
WooCommerce module that wires in automatically when WooCommerce is active. Neither one trusts a
tool’s own “read-only” or “safe” label; classification comes from the plugin’s own policy map.

Capability packs and tiers

Every governed ability maps to a tier: reversible (read), side-effecting (write), or
irreversible (delete, refund, cancel). A capability pack is a named, scoped view of the verb
catalog for one identity — a WordPress application password, a user or role, or a WooCommerce
REST API key — with an allow list, a hard-denied tier class, a per-tier approval requirement, and
optional rate and spend limits. A credential with no explicit binding falls back to a safe
default pack rather than inheriting full access.

Human approval

When a pack requires approval for a tier (the starter packs do for irreversible calls), a call
at that tier doesn’t execute. It is queued under Tools → Pending Agent Actions for a human
to approve or reject. When an
Approval is requested, Belayline Agent Governance captures a fingerprint of the target’s current state; when
the approval is claimed, it re-checks that fingerprint. A mismatch means the target changed
between request and claim, so the old approval is marked stale and a fresh request is filed. This
narrows the gap between a human’s approval and the write — it does not close it, because the
short window between claiming an approval and executing the call still exists.

Self-service approval status

An agent can call belayline/check-approval with an approval_id to poll its own request
without a human in the loop. It reports a reduced, public status (pending, approved, rejected,
expired, used, or superseded) and a plain-English next_action, and never returns the approver’s
identity, the original arguments, or any token.

Hash-chained audit log

Every gate decision and executed action is appended to an append-only, hash-chained log under
Tools → Agent Audit Log, with a tamper-evidence check that re-verifies the chain on load.

Core coverage

Governs the three abilities WordPress core registers today. Any other core/* ability is denied
until Belayline Agent Governance maps it, so future core write abilities fail closed rather than run
ungoverned.

WooCommerce coverage

When WooCommerce is active, Belayline Agent Governance governs exactly these 16 abilities:

  • woocommerce/products-list
  • woocommerce/products-get
  • woocommerce/products-create
  • woocommerce/products-update
  • woocommerce/products-delete
  • woocommerce/products-query
  • woocommerce/product-create
  • woocommerce/product-update
  • woocommerce/product-delete
  • woocommerce/orders-list
  • woocommerce/orders-get
  • woocommerce/orders-create
  • woocommerce/orders-update
  • woocommerce/orders-query
  • woocommerce/order-add-note
  • woocommerce/order-update-status

Everything else under woocommerce/ is refused as an unknown verb. Deleting a product with
force: true is classed irreversible; a plain delete (trash) is side-effecting.

Which MCP endpoint to use

WooCommerce’s own MCP endpoint (/wp-json/woocommerce/mcp) is deprecated by WooCommerce itself,
which points clients at the shared mcp-adapter server instead. Belayline Agent Governance governs both the
same way, through the ability permission check, but the two endpoints don’t expose the same
information to an agent:

  • On the shared mcp-adapter server, an agent that hits approval_required gets the full error
    data, including approval_id, and can call belayline/check-approval to poll it.
  • On WooCommerce’s own endpoint, the bundled mcp-adapter 0.3.0 only forwards the error message
    text to the client, not the structured error data. An agent sees the message “needs human
    approval” but not the approval_id, and belayline/check-approval isn’t reachable on that
    transport at all — the approval still exists and is visible on the Pending Actions page, but
    the agent can’t self-serve it.

We recommend running agents against the shared mcp-adapter server. WooCommerce’s own endpoint is
supported for as long as WooCommerce ships it, with the limitation above.

Environment awareness

Belayline Agent Governance notices when a site’s address changes (a migration, a staging clone) and treats it
as a new environment: shadow-mode windows, active grants, and approved-but-unclaimed approvals
are all voided rather than carried over silently, and an admin notice stays up until someone
rebinds the site from the settings page. Production sites (wp_get_environment_type() ===
'production', WordPress’s own default) never default to shadow mode and cap any shadow window at
24 hours.

Multisite

WordPress multisite is not supported. Activation is refused on a multisite install, network-wide
or per site.

External services

This plugin can send data outside your site in two ways.

Email. When a new agent action needs approval, Belayline Agent Governance sends an email through
wp_mail() to the site’s admin email address, or to a recipient set on the Pending Agent
Actions screen, linking to the login-protected review screen. It goes through your site’s own
mail delivery.

Webhook (opt-in). An administrator can set a webhook URL on the Pending Agent Actions
screen. When
set, every new pending approval sends an HTTP POST to that URL with a JSON body containing the
event name, the approval id, the verb (ability) that was called, and a link to the review screen.
No call arguments are sent. The webhook is off until an administrator enters a URL, and the
destination is the site operator’s choice. Nothing is sent to the plugin’s author.

Privacy

Belayline Agent Governance keeps a hash-chained audit log of gate decisions and executed agent actions,
including the identity that made the call. A personal-data export for a WordPress user includes
their matching audit rows. An erasure request does not delete them: they are reported as
retained, with a note that they’re kept as a tamper-evident security record, because rewriting a
row would break the hash chain that proves the log hasn’t been tampered with. Matching is done by
resolving the requester’s email to a WordPress user and matching rows on that user only; recorded
tool inputs are never searched for personal data, but they may contain it, since they can include
data handled by other plugins (customer records, order details) that the calling agent’s tool
touched.
belayline-agent-governance.installation:
1. Upload the plugin to /wp-content/plugins/belayline-agent-governance, or install it through the Plugins
    screen.
  2. Activate Belayline Agent Governance.
  3. Visit Tools → Agent Capability Packs to bind identities (application passwords, users or
    roles, WooCommerce REST API keys) to a pack. Unbound credentials get a safe default pack.
  4. Review pending actions under Tools → Pending Agent Actions and the log under Tools →
    Agent Audit Log    .

WooCommerce support activates automatically when WooCommerce is active; there is nothing else to
configure for it to be safe by default.
belayline-agent-governance.faq:
Does this require WooCommerce?

No. The plugin is WordPress-general and governs the core Abilities API on any site. WooCommerce
support is a self-contained module that loads only when WooCommerce is active.

Does it work on multisite?

No. Activation is refused on a multisite install, both network-wide and per site.

What about WooCommerce’s own MCP endpoint?

It’s governed the same way as the shared mcp-adapter server, but WooCommerce’s bundled
mcp-adapter version doesn’t forward the structured approval_required error data to the client,
so an agent on that endpoint can see the approval message but not the approval_id, and can’t
reach belayline/check-approval. See the Description for details. We recommend the shared
mcp-adapter server; WooCommerce’s own endpoint is supported while WooCommerce continues to ship
it.

What happens to my data on uninstall?

Nothing, by default. Deleting the plugin from the Plugins screen leaves the audit log, approval
tables, and plugin options in place, because the audit log is a tamper-evident security record.
To have uninstall remove everything (all three tables, every option, every scheduled cron event),
define BELAYLINE_REMOVE_DATA as true (for example in wp-config.php) before deleting the
plugin.

How are AI agents identified?

By whichever credential authenticated the request: a WordPress application password, a logged-in
user or their role, or — when WooCommerce is active — the WooCommerce REST API key used to
authenticate the request. Each is bound to a capability pack independently under Tools → Agent
Capability Packs.

pairly-connect.description:
Pairly Connect links this WordPress site to your Pairly workspace. Once connected, you and the AI workers in Pairly can draft, schedule and publish posts on this site, without copying anything across by hand.

WordPress stays the source of truth. Posts are stored here as normal WordPress posts, so anything you edit in WordPress is what Pairly sees next.

What Pairly can do on your site

  • Read your posts, including drafts
  • Create and edit drafts
  • Publish, schedule and unpublish posts
  • Add the images a post uses to your Media Library, and set featured images
  • Set SEO titles, descriptions and social previews. They are written to Yoast SEO or Rank Math when either is active.

What Pairly cannot do

Pairly cannot install or change plugins or themes, see or manage users, change site settings, or delete posts. The plugin exposes only its own post tools; nothing else on your site is reachable through the connection.

How the connection works

  • An administrator approves the connection on a WordPress screen, much like signing in with Google. Pairly never sees your WordPress password.
  • The connection uses OAuth 2.1 with PKCE. Access tokens expire after an hour, and they are stored only as hashes.
  • Pairly acts with the permissions of the administrator who approved it, and only through this plugin’s endpoint. A Pairly token cannot be used anywhere else on your site’s REST API.
  • You can disconnect at any time from Settings → Pairly Connect. Access ends immediately.

Requirements

  • The site must be served over HTTPS and reachable from the internet.
  • WordPress must be installed at the root of its domain (example.com, not example.com/blog).
  • Your web server must pass /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server through to WordPress. Almost every host does; the settings page checks it for you.

External services

This plugin connects your site to Pairly, a service run by Pairly. It is needed so your Pairly workspace can manage posts on this site.

  • When you click “Connect to Pairly”, your browser opens the Pairly app (https://app.pairlyhq.com), with your site’s address in the link, so Pairly can start the connection.
  • When you approve the connection, Pairly registers itself with your site and receives an access token. From then on, Pairly’s servers (https://api.pairlyhq.com) call this site’s endpoint (/wp-json/pairly/v1/mcp) to read and write posts. They send and receive post content, SEO fields and tags. Your site does not send data to Pairly on its own; it only answers Pairly’s requests.
  • When Pairly publishes a post that has images, your site downloads those images from Pairly’s media storage into your Media Library.

The plugin sends no analytics or tracking data, and makes no requests while it is not connected, apart from checking its own address on the settings page.

Pairly terms and conditions and privacy policy.

Credits

Bundles the WordPress MCP Adapter (GPLv2 or later) and the Space Grotesk and DM Sans typefaces (SIL Open Font License 1.1, see assets/fonts/OFL.txt).
pairly-connect.installation:
1. Install and activate Pairly Connect from Plugins → Add New.
  2. You are taken to Settings → Pairly Connect. If anything needs fixing first, such as HTTPS, the page tells you what to do.
  3. Click Connect to Pairly and sign in to your Pairly workspace.
  4. Back in WordPress, review what Pairly will be able to do, then click Approve.
pairly-connect.faq:
Do I need a Pairly account?

Yes. Pairly Connect links your site to a Pairly workspace, so you need one to connect.

Will Pairly change my existing posts?

Only when you, or an AI worker in your Pairly workspace, edit or publish a post. Publishing from AI workers goes through approval in Pairly by default. Pairly cannot delete posts.

What happens to formatting Pairly does not understand?

Blocks Pairly cannot edit, such as galleries, embeds or columns, are kept exactly as they are. They show in Pairly as a placeholder you can keep or remove, and your WordPress markup is never rewritten unless you change that block.

Does it work with Yoast SEO or Rank Math?

Yes. SEO titles, descriptions, canonical URLs, robots settings and social previews set in Pairly are written to whichever of the two is active, and edits made in them are what Pairly reads back.

How do I disconnect?

Go to Settings → Pairly Connect and click Disconnect. Every token is revoked at once. Disconnecting from inside Pairly revokes access too.

Does it work on multisite?

Each site in a network connects separately, from its own Settings → Pairly Connect page.

raqvio-agent-guardrails.description:
AI agents can now work on your WordPress site directly. Since WordPress 6.9, plugins register abilities — “update a product”, “change an order status” — and agents such as Claude Desktop or your own scripts can discover and run them over the REST API or MCP. WooCommerce exposes products and orders this way too.

That is powerful, and a little unnerving. Out of the box there is no way to say “this agent may read orders but never refund one”, no off switch, and no record of what an agent actually did.

Raqvio Agent Guardrails adds that missing layer. It sits in front of every ability your site runs, works out which agent is calling, decides whether the call is allowed, and writes it down.

Features

  • See every ability on your site. Abilities from WordPress, WooCommerce and other plugins are listed in one place, each classified as Read, Write, Financial or Destructive. Disagree with a classification? Override it. Mark an ability as sensitive and its input is never logged.
  • Name your agents. Tie an application password, or a dedicated WordPress user, to a named agent. Add as many agents as you need. A built-in “Site AI” agent covers AI features running inside WordPress.
  • Allow or deny per agent. Choose, ability by ability, what each agent may do. Agents you haven’t set up get safe defaults: they can read, but anything that writes, moves money or deletes is denied.
  • An emergency kill switch. One click in the admin bar blocks every agent at once. From the dashboard you can also block agents for one hour, after which the switch turns itself off.
  • A redacted audit log. Every agent call is recorded with the agent, the channel (MCP, REST or internal), the decision and the result. Before anything is stored, values in fields named like passwords, tokens, keys or card data are removed, and emails, phone numbers and addresses are masked. You choose how long entries are kept, from 1 to 365 days (30 by default).
  • A credential and exposure check. Find out whether your AI provider keys live in the database or safely in wp-config.php or environment variables — without Raqvio Agent Guardrails ever reading them — plus which abilities are publicly exposed and which administrators have application passwords.
  • A catalog readiness score. With WooCommerce, scan your catalog and get a 0–100 score per product and for the store, based on what AI shopping agents need: descriptions, images and alt text, SKU, GTIN/MPN/brand, attributes, variations, price and stock, and title quality. A separate check tells you whether your product pages carry Product JSON-LD.
  • Help for well-behaved agents. The raqvio-ag/get-my-permissions ability lets an agent ask what it is allowed to do before it tries.
  • A refund ability that stays under your control. raqvio-ag/order-create-refund (WooCommerce 10.9 or newer) lets an agent refund an order by amount or per line item, with optional restock. It is classified as Financial, so no agent can use it until you allow it, and money only goes back through the payment gateway if the agent explicitly asks and the gateway supports automatic refunds.
  • Works with WooCommerce’s MCP endpoint. Agents that connect with WooCommerce REST API keys are identified by the key’s user, and WooCommerce’s MCP tools show up in the permission matrix like any other ability.

When an agent is blocked it gets a clear error (raqvio_ag_denied, or raqvio_ag_blocked while the kill switch is on) with a reason that starts with “Blocked by Raqvio Agent Guardrails:”, so both the agent and you know why.

Requirements

Raqvio Agent Guardrails needs WordPress 6.9 and PHP 8.1. To actually block agents it needs WordPress 7.1, which added the hook Raqvio Agent Guardrails uses to stop an ability before it runs. On WordPress 6.9 and 7.0 it runs in audit-only mode: it logs every agent call and what it would have decided, and tells you so.

WooCommerce is optional. Governance works for any ability; the catalog readiness score and the refund ability need WooCommerce.

Privacy

Everything Raqvio Agent Guardrails stores stays in your own database:

  • Audit log: time, agent, WordPress user ID, channel, ability, risk, decision, status, duration, a short result summary, and the ability input after redaction (see above). Abilities you mark as sensitive never have their input stored. Entries older than the retention period you set in Settings (30 days by default) are deleted automatically.
  • Agents: name, description, status, and the ID of the bound application password or user. The application password itself is never read or stored.
  • Catalog readiness: a score and a list of issues per product.

Source code and libraries

The compiled admin app in build/ is generated from the readable JavaScript and SCSS sources included in this plugin under assets/src/. The build configuration (package.json and webpack.config.js) is included too. To rebuild it, run npm install and then npm run build in the plugin folder (Node.js 20 or newer). The build uses @wordpress/scripts.

Bundled third-party libraries:

  • Action Scheduler 4.2.0 by WooCommerce (GPLv3), in vendor/woocommerce/action-scheduler/. It runs background jobs when WooCommerce is not active. If another plugin loads a newer copy, Action Scheduler uses that one.
  • Freemius WordPress SDK 2.13.4 (GPLv3), in freemius/. Its compiled pricing page script, freemius/assets/js/pricing/freemius-pricing.js, is built from github.com/Freemius/pricing-page. When several plugins bundle the SDK, it loads only the newest copy.
raqvio-agent-guardrails.installation:
1. Install Raqvio Agent Guardrails from Plugins → Add New Plugin and activate it. On multisite, activate it on each site rather than network-wide.
  2. Open Raqvio Agent Guardrails → Settings and look through the hardening checklist at the bottom.
  3. Create a dedicated WordPress user for your agent. Give it only the capabilities the agent needs — Raqvio Agent Guardrails narrows what a user can do, it never grants capabilities. The “AI Agent (Raqvio Agent Guardrails)” role is a read-only starting point; a role such as Shop Manager lets an agent work with products and orders.
  4. Edit that user and create an application password for the agent.
  5. In Raqvio Agent Guardrails → Agents, click Add agent, bind it to that application password, then open Permissions and allow what the agent should be able to do.
  6. Connect your AI client with the user name and application password, through the WordPress Abilities REST API (/wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/) or an MCP server. Your agent’s calls appear in Raqvio Agent Guardrails → Audit Log.

Using WooCommerce’s MCP endpoint instead? Bind the agent to the WordPress user who owns the WooCommerce API key. Step-by-step guides, including a tested Claude Desktop setup, are at guardrails.raqvio.com/docs.
raqvio-agent-guardrails.faq:
Does Raqvio Agent Guardrails work without WooCommerce?

Yes. It governs any ability registered through the WordPress Abilities API. The catalog readiness score and the refund ability simply don’t appear until WooCommerce is active.

Are people using wp-admin affected?

No, not by default. Raqvio Agent Guardrails only governs agent traffic: calls made with an application password or over MCP, users with the “AI Agent (Raqvio Agent Guardrails)” role, and the built-in Site AI. If you want logged-in people to follow the same rules, turn on “Govern all ability executions” in Settings.

What happens to agents I haven’t set up?

They are treated as unknown agents and get the defaults from Settings: Read abilities are allowed; Write, Financial and Destructive ones are denied. You can change each of those.

Why don’t I see my agent’s calls in the audit log?

Make sure the calls really come from an agent. A request from your own logged-in browser session isn’t governed unless “Govern all ability executions” is on. On WordPress 6.9 and 7.0, entries are marked “(not enforced)” because nothing can be blocked yet.

Can agents issue refunds?

Only if you let them. The refund ability is Financial, so it is denied until you allow it for a specific agent. By default a refund is only recorded in WooCommerce; it returns money through the payment gateway only when the agent asks for that and the gateway supports it. Developers can remove the ability entirely with add_filter( 'raqvio_ag_register_refund_ability', '__return_false' );.

Can a refund be undone?

No. Refunds and payments are final, and Raqvio Agent Guardrails says so wherever it matters. If you want a person to look at larger refunds first, Raqvio Agent Guardrails Pro can hold them for approval.

Can an agent switch off its own guardrails?

No. Raqvio Agent Guardrails’s settings can only be changed from a logged-in wp-admin session of someone allowed to manage Raqvio Agent Guardrails. Requests made with an application password are always refused, even for administrator accounts.

Does Raqvio Agent Guardrails read my AI API keys?

No. The hardening check only reports where a key is configured — environment variable, wp-config.php constant, or database. For the database it runs a LENGTH() query, so the key itself never leaves MySQL.

Will it slow my site down?

Raqvio Agent Guardrails only does work when an ability runs. Its policies are compiled and cached, and the test suite checks that the overhead per call stays under 5 ms at the 95th percentile, including writing the audit entry.

What happens to my data if I delete the plugin?

Deactivating keeps everything. Deleting the plugin keeps your data too, unless you first turn on “Delete all Raqvio Agent Guardrails data when the plugin is uninstalled” in Settings.

agentdesk-site-operations.description:
Agentdesk Site Operations connects MCP-capable AI clients (such as Claude, Cursor, and VS Code) to your WordPress site through a fixed, predefined set of operations built on WordPress’s own APIs. Ask in plain language and your agent performs the operation.

This plugin does not edit files, execute code, run arbitrary SQL, or install other plugins. Every action is one of a fixed set of reviewed operations that go through core WordPress functions (wp_insert_post, wp_update_post, the WooCommerce CRUD APIs, and Elementor’s own document meta). There is no file manager and no code editor.

Content is filtered with wp_kses_post, and the Elementor HTML and Shortcode widgets are rejected, unless the acting user holds the unfiltered_html capability – the same rule WordPress itself applies in the block and classic editors.

What you can do

  • Content – create, edit, publish, search, and organize posts, pages, and custom post types; manage categories, tags, and comments.
  • Media – browse the library, import images from a URL, and edit titles/alt text.
  • WooCommerce – create, update and delete products; update order status and add order notes; list variations, coupons, customers and sales reports.
  • Elementor – list pages, read and update the Elementor document (structured widget data), add headings/text/buttons/containers, and build pages from a brief.
  • SEO – read and update Yoast / Rank Math SEO meta for posts you can edit.
  • Site settings – read and update a small allowlist of general options (site title, tagline, date/time format, posts per page). Site address, home URL and admin email are deliberately excluded.
  • Maintenance – flush page and object caches; detect installed integrations.
  • Read & audit – site info, health checks, environment diagnostics, user and plugin/theme inventory, debug configuration, and an action log.

The plugin does not create users, change roles, or modify user passwords.

Predefined operations, by design

Every tool is a fixed operation with a typed input schema. The agent cannot write files, edit theme or plugin code, run raw database queries, or install software. This keeps the surface small, reviewable, and safe.

Safety

  • Authentication – a bcrypt-hashed API key or a WordPress Application Password is required on every request.
  • Capability checks – each operation runs as a real WordPress user. Content operations are checked per object (you cannot edit or delete an item you could not edit in wp-admin), and internal or block-theme template post types are never writable.
  • Safe mode (default on) – blocks permanently destructive operations such as deleting posts, media, products and comments.
  • Power mode (default off) – required for sensitive operations: site settings, and overwriting or importing an Elementor document.
  • Rate limiting – a per-IP flood guard plus a per-key request budget.
  • Audit log – every action is recorded.

Self-hosted

Runs entirely on your site. No external service and no account: nothing is sent to us or to any third-party service. Your own AI client connects directly to your site.
agentdesk-site-operations.installation:
1. Install and activate Agentdesk Site Operations.
  2. Go to Settings > Agentdesk Site Operations and click Create API Key (shown once – copy it).
  3. Add the endpoint and key to your MCP client:
    https://your-site.com/wp-json/agentdesk-site-operations/v1/mcp
  4. Enable Power Mode only when you need site settings or Elementor document overwrites; keep Safe Mode on.
agentdesk-site-operations.faq:
Does it edit files or run code?

No. There is no file editor, file manager, or code execution. Every action is a fixed, predefined operation through WordPress’s own APIs.

Does it send my data anywhere?

No. It is entirely self-hosted; your agent connects to your site and nothing leaves your server.

Which AI clients work with it?

Any client that speaks MCP over HTTP with a Bearer token, such as Claude, Cursor, and VS Code.

sm-bot-flagger.description:
Most analytics trust what a visitor says it is. Attack tools know that, so they call themselves Chrome, or Googlebot, or an AI crawler, and walk straight past. SM Bot Flagger checks what they actually do: a request for your cloud credentials is an attack, whatever name it gives.

What it does

Each front-end request is written to its own table with:

  • date and time, in site time and UTC
  • IP address, stored whole or masked
  • user agent
  • referrer and referring domain
  • requested path and query string
  • HTTP status code
  • whether the request started a new visit, which makes it a landing page
  • the category and client name the rules assigned
  • how long WordPress took to build the page

Nothing is written to postmeta, and there is one INSERT per request.

Categories

Traffic is sorted into six buckets:

  • Regular traffic — looks like a person in a browser
  • Search bots — Googlebot, Bingbot, DuckDuckBot and friends
  • AI bots — GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Bytespider, CCBot and around thirty others
  • Malicious traffic — sqlmap, Nikto, WPScan, plus around 75 path signatures:
    config and env files, backup leftovers, SSH and private keys, AWS, Azure,
    Google Cloud, Oracle, OVH, Linode and Hetzner credentials, Docker and
    Kubernetes, Terraform state, Vite and Spring Actuator file disclosure, path
    traversal and SQL injection, and credential files for AI coding agents
  • Other bots — SEO crawlers, uptime monitors, link previews, HTTP libraries
  • Caching — your own cache plugins warming pages: WP Rocket preload and bot,
    WP Fastest Cache, LiteSpeed crawler, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache,
    FlyingPress, NitroPack, Cache Enabler, Swift Performance, Cloudflare Always
    Online
  • Unclassified — empty or unrecognised user agents

Cache warming is the site requesting its own pages, so it is not a visit and it
is not really a bot either. Keeping it separate stops preload runs from inflating
the traffic numbers. Filter the log to Caching to check a preload actually ran.

Settings has a “Do not log” row where you can tick categories to discard. Those
requests are still classified, then dropped before anything is written, so they
cost one pass over the rules and no database queries at all. This is worth doing
for Caching on a busy site, where a preload run can easily be the largest source
of requests. Nothing is stored, so skipped traffic cannot be recovered later and
will not show up in the log, the charts or the API.

A rule matches on one of three things: the user agent, the request path, or the
IP address. User agent and path patterns match anywhere in the value, with *
as a wildcard and an optional regular expression. Address patterns understand an
exact address, a prefix such as 203.0.113, a wildcard such as 203.0.113.*, and
CIDR ranges such as 203.0.113.0/24 or 2001:db8::/32. Prefixes only match on a
boundary, so 192.168.1 will not match 192.168.10.4.

This is how you handle a crawler that lies about its user agent, or a scraper
running from one hosting range: match the address instead. It is also how you
mark an internal monitoring path or a staging endpoint as something other than
real traffic.

Rules live under SM Bot Flagger → Classification. Each rule matches a substring
or a regular expression against the user agent, the path or the IP. They are
evaluated top to bottom and the first match wins, so put narrow rules above broad
ones. You can edit, reorder, disable, delete and restore them.

Performance

Bot Flagger → Performance shows how long WordPress takes to build your pages, from the build time already recorded with every request:

  • the typical page (median) and the slowest 5%, compared with the period before
  • a chart per day, or per hour for the last 24 hours
  • the slowest pages, each linking to its requests in the traffic log
  • build times per visitor type, so you can see whether bots get slower pages

It starts with Regular traffic only, and you can add any other visitor type. The Dashboard has a small Performance card that follows its own filters. Pages served from a page cache never reach WordPress, so they are not measured.

Privacy

SM Bot Flagger processes personal data in the sense of the GDPR, because an IP
address is personal data. The defaults are chosen to keep as little as
possible:

  • IP addresses are masked before storage, to /24 for IPv4 and /48 for IPv6.
    Full addresses are stored only if you switch that on.
  • Visitors are counted through a hash of the masked address, the user agent
    and a secret that changes every day, so nobody can be followed from one day
    to the next.
  • Values that look like secrets in URLs, such as password reset keys and
    tokens, are removed before a row is written.
  • Administrators are not logged by default.
  • Entries are deleted after 90 days by default.
  • Nothing leaves your server. There is no tracking script, no external
    service, no call home. The plugin author never sees your data.

The plugin adds suggested text to your site’s privacy policy guide under
Settings > Privacy > Policy Guide. Adapt it to your configuration. If you
store full addresses or keep entries longer, say so there, and check your
legal basis: for most sites that is a legitimate interest in security, which
should be recorded in your processing register.

The optional MCP endpoint lets a tool you connect read the log. Whoever holds
a token can read the same data you can, so treat tokens as passwords and
revoke the ones you no longer use.

The MCP endpoint

Enable it under Settings, then create a token under MCP API.

Endpoint: https://your-site.tld/wp-json/sm-bot-flagger/v1/mcp
Transport: streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0 over POST
Auth: Authorization: Bearer <token>, or X-MCP-Token: <token> if a proxy
strips the Authorization header

Tools:

  • get_traffic_summary — totals and the category split for a period
  • get_timeseries — hourly or daily counts per category
  • get_top — ranks pages, landing pages, referrers, referring domains, user
    agents, clients, categories, status codes, IPs, rules or hour of day
  • search_hits — individual requests, with filters
  • classify_user_agent — test a user agent against the current rules
  • list_classification_rules — the rules in evaluation order
  • upsert_classification_rule — add or change a rule, write token only
  • delete_classification_rule — remove a rule, write token only

Read tokens can only read. Give a token write access only if you want the client
to change how traffic is categorised.

If Authorization never arrives, add this to .htaccess on Apache:

SetEnvIf Authorization "(.*)" HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=$1

Hooks

Extension points for add-ons:

sm_bot_flagger_categories (array) — add your own traffic categories. They appear in the

rules editor, the charts, the filters and the MCP schemas automatically.
sm_bot_flagger_classification (array) — override the category, label or rule for a
request, after the rules have run.
sm_bot_flagger_mcp_tools (array) — register MCP tools. Include a callback key and the
free plugin will dispatch to it.
sm_bot_flagger_stats_where (array) — append conditions to every stats query.
sm_bot_flagger_admin_menu (action) — add a submenu page under SM Bot Flagger.
sm_bot_flagger_dashboard_cards / sm_bot_flagger_dashboard_panels (actions) — add to the dashboard.
sm_bot_flagger_log_columns (array) and sm_bot_flagger_log_column (action) — add columns to the log.
sm_bot_flagger_settings_fields (action) and sm_bot_flagger_sanitize_settings (array) — add settings.

SM_Bot_Flagger_Logger::current_classification() classifies the current request once and

caches it, so an add-on can act on a crawler early rather than at shutdown.

sm_bot_flagger_should_log (bool) — return false to skip logging a request.
sm_bot_flagger_hit_data (array) — change the row before it is written, or return an empty

array to drop it. Useful for adding a country lookup.
sm_bot_flagger_mcp_tools (array) — add your own MCP tools. Give each one a handler named
tool_ on a class of your choosing and hook tools/call accordingly.

Notes on accuracy

  • Logging happens on shutdown, so requests served entirely from a page cache
    or a CDN never reach PHP and are not counted. On a cached site, treat these
    numbers as a lower bound.
  • Bot detection relies on self-reported user agents. Anything determined to look
    like a browser will be counted as regular traffic.
  • Only pick a proxy header for the IP if a proxy actually sets it. A client can
    send X-Forwarded-For itself, which would let anyone forge their address.

Security notes

  • Query string values for parameters like key, token, code, password and nonce
    are replaced with [redacted] before a row is written, so password reset links
    and OAuth callbacks do not end up sitting in the log table.
  • CSV exports prefix any cell starting with =, +, – or @ with an apostrophe, so
    a crafted user agent cannot run as a formula when the file is opened.
  • The MCP endpoint blocks an address for 15 minutes after 20 failed token
    attempts.
  • Tokens are not accepted as a ?token= query parameter by default, because
    query strings leak into access logs and referrers. Enable it with the
    sm_bot_flagger_mcp_allow_query_token filter if a client cannot send headers.
  • A regular expression that does not compile is switched off rather than being
    treated as literal text, so a typo cannot silently widen what a rule matches.
  • Rule patterns are matched against at most the first 1000 characters of a
    header, which bounds the cost of a badly written expression.

A write-scoped MCP token can change classification rules, and those rules run on
every front-end request. Treat a write token as trusted, and hand out read
tokens for anything that only needs to look at the numbers.

Behaviour rules

Pattern rules judge a request on what it looks like. Behaviour rules judge a
client on what it has been doing. They run at log time, because they need the
response status and a short memory, and they need a stored IP address, so they
do nothing when IP storage is off. Confirmed search and AI crawlers are never
demoted by them.

Random paths. A 404 on a single path segment of 4 to 12 alphanumeric characters
with no vowels and mixed case, such as /6bXX29bt, is treated as scanning. Real
slugs contain vowels; generated tokens do not. The 404 is required, so a short
consonant heavy page of your own is never caught.

Repeated 404s. Flagged on both a count and a share: by default 8 misses within
10 minutes, and at least half of that client’s requests in the window missing.
The share is what makes this safe. A busy legitimate client can collect a
handful of 404s among hundreds of good requests, and counting alone would flag
it. Scanners miss on almost everything they ask for.

Login attempts. A cumulative count of requests to wp-login.php and xmlrpc.php,
10 per hour by default. Deliberately not a rate: credential stuffing is usually
slow and spread over many addresses, so a per-second limit never sees it.

Request rate, off by default. On real traffic the fastest clients are usually
legitimate, while scanners and credential stuffing run slowly enough to pass any
threshold worth setting. Counting 404s separates the two far better than
counting requests. Measure your own traffic before switching this on.

Once a client trips a rule it stays flagged for an hour by default, and what it
already did in that window is recategorised too.

Path precedence

A user agent is a claim the client makes about itself. Anything can send
“OAI-SearchBot” or “Googlebot”, and plenty of attack tooling does, because it
gets past naive filtering.

Settings has “Trust the path”, on by default, which tests path and address rules
before user agent rules. A request for /root/.aws/credentials is then recorded
as an attack whatever it claims to be, and your genuine crawler rules stay
correct for genuine crawlers.

Turn it off if you would rather rules were evaluated strictly in the order shown
on the Classification screen.

Filtering

Dashboard tiles toggle categories, and several can be combined. Rows in the top
lists are links: click a page, landing page, status code, client or referring
domain to open the traffic log filtered to it.

The log itself filters on category, status family (2xx to 5xx), an exact status
code, a page path, landing pages only, and a free text search across path, user
agent, referrer, IP and client. Combining a path with “landing pages only” gives
you the entry traffic for one page. Filters survive paging and are applied to
CSV exports.

Correcting a classification

Open the Traffic log and click the client name on any row. You get the user
agent as an editable pattern, a name, and a category. Shorten the pattern to the
distinctive part before saving, for example MyScraper/2. rather than the whole
string, so the rule catches other versions too.

Saving puts the rule first in the evaluation order, so it beats the shipped
defaults. Tick the box to also rewrite requests that are already in the log,
which is matched on the user agent containing your pattern.

The chart above the table follows the filters, and can be grouped by category,
by client or by the raw user agent. The eight busiest values get their own band
and the rest are folded into “Everything else”. “Show full user agent” prints
the whole string under each client name.
sm-bot-flagger.installation:
1. Install through Plugins > Add New, or upload the zip.
  2. Activate. Logging starts straight away with privacy-friendly defaults.
  3. Open SM Bot Flagger in the admin menu. The dashboard fills as traffic arrives.
  4. Optional: under Settings, turn on the MCP endpoint and create a token to
    connect Claude or another MCP client.
sm-bot-flagger.faq:
Will it slow my site down?

Logging happens at the very end of each request, as one database write.
Behaviour rules only keep counters for clients that have already requested a
missing page.

Does it work with page caching?

Pages served straight from a cache never reach WordPress, so they are not
logged. On a heavily cached site, read the numbers as a floor rather than a
total. Your cache plugin’s own warming requests are recognised and kept out
of your visitor numbers.

Is it GDPR compliant?

It is built to keep as little as possible: masked addresses, a visitor hash
that changes daily, secrets removed from URLs, administrators excluded, and
90-day retention. See the Privacy section. Compliance also depends on how you
run your site: adapt the suggested privacy policy text, and record your legal
basis.

Does any data leave my server?

No. There is no tracking script, no external service and no call home. The
plugin author never sees your traffic.

What is the MCP endpoint?

A small server inside WordPress that lets an AI assistant or any MCP client
read the traffic log and ask questions in plain language. It is off by
default, needs a token you create, and read-only tokens cannot change
anything.

Can I correct a classification?

Yes. Click a client in the traffic log, choose the category, and optionally
match on the path or address instead of the user agent. Past requests are
corrected too.

Is there a paid version?

Yes. The Pro add-on adds verified crawlers, so a fake Googlebot is caught by
DNS rather than by name; blocking by category, behaviour or address, with a
monitor mode; and priority support. See https://seomarketeer.eu.

Where do I get help?

In this plugin’s support forum on WordPress.org, or through
https://seomarketeer.eu.

everybooking.description:
Turn “request a quote” into an instant quote your customer can book.

A couple planning a wedding wants to know what their day will cost. On most venue websites they fill in a contact form and wait days for a reply, and many book somewhere else in the meantime. With Everybooking they pick their date, guest numbers and extras on your website and see the full price straight away: the venue hire, the dinner, the rooms for the family. If the date is free, they can book it and pay the deposit in the same visit.

The same works for anyone whose price depends on dates, times, nights, headcount or quantity. Everybooking works out the price from your own rates and your live availability and shows the customer a real quote, 4 seconds on average after they have entered the details your pricing needs. This plugin puts that on your WordPress site: inside any page, or behind a “Get an Instant Quote” button that opens it over the page you are on.

It is free to start: an Everybooking account costs nothing, needs no credit card, has no time limit and includes 50 quotes. Build your free quote page.

Who it is for

  • Wedding and event venues: the venue by date, dinner by guest, rooms by night, with your packages, minimums and deposits.
  • Retreat centers and lodging: rooms, meals and meeting space priced by night and by head, with seasonal rates.
  • Equipment and vehicle rentals: by the day or week, by quantity, with each unit tracked so nothing goes out twice.
  • Tour and activity operators: by time slot and party size.
  • Service businesses: caterers, builders, plumbers, removal firms and anyone else who quotes by the hour, the guest or the job.

See it working

Live example pages, each with a real booking page you can try (nothing is booked):

  • A wedding venue: the barn and orchard, priced by date and guest numbers.
  • A builder: kitchens, bathrooms and extensions estimated before anyone visits.
  • A caterer: the menu, guest numbers and hours, priced straight away.
  • A plumber: describe the job and see the price before the visit.
  • A removal firm: fixed price or hourly, side by side.
  • A theatre box office: pick a show and choose your seats.

The example site is built with Wix; this plugin puts the same booking pages and quote buttons on a WordPress site.

A quote button where your visitors already look

Most sites send people to a quote from a button near the top of the home page. Your theme or page builder made that button, so this plugin does not try to replace it. Instead, any of these opens your booking page in a full-screen pop-up, without the visitor leaving your site:

  • Your own buttons. Set the link of any button or menu item to #instant-quote (or #everybooking-your-page). Works in Elementor, Divi, Beaver Builder, Astra, the block editor and menus, with no code.
  • A floating button on every page, at the bottom of the screen or as a bar across it, in your theme’s button colour or one you choose. One switch. On a page about one service it opens that service’s booking page.
  • The Everybooking Quote Button block and the [everybooking_button] shortcode, each opening the booking page you pick.

The pop-up fills the screen on phones, closes with the close button, Escape or the phone’s Back button, and keeps the visitor’s progress if they close it and come back.

As many booking pages as you like

Show one booking page or fifty: weddings on one page, corporate events on another, a “Plan your wedding” and a “Book a venue tour” button side by side, or the same booking page at the top and the bottom of a long page. In Settings → Everybooking, choose Add on each booking page you want, as many times as you want, put them in order and create the page in one click.

Ready for AI assistants (MCP)

This plugin works with the WordPress MCP Adapter. Install it, and Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any assistant that speaks MCP (the Model Context Protocol) can work with your booking pages for you: list them, put any number of them on a new page or an existing one, set the default, and switch on the quote button. Ask “Put our three tour booking pages on a new page called Tours, as buttons”, and it is done as a draft for you to check. The assistant acts as you, with your WordPress permissions, and never sees your Everybooking connection key. Needs WordPress 6.9 or newer.

Why it is different from a booking calendar or a quote form

  • A real price, not an estimate. Rates by the hour, time slot, day, night and quantity, with your fees, discounts and deposits, added up on the spot.
  • Live availability. Every quote checks your actual inventory, down to the individual room, vehicle or piece of equipment.
  • Quote, book and pay in one visit. The quote continues into booking and the deposit or payment options you have set up.
  • Built for you by AI. Give Everybooking your website address and it drafts your quote page. On Growth plans you can change it by talking to Claude, ChatGPT or Grok through MCP (the Model Context Protocol), with no WordPress access needed.
  • One source of truth. Prices, inventory, quotes and bookings live in your Everybooking account. Change a rate there and your WordPress page shows it. There is nothing to sync and no second calendar.

What you get

  • An Everybooking Instant Quote & Booking block for the block editor, with a view-only preview.
  • An Everybooking Quote Button block that opens a booking page in a pop-up.
  • [everybooking] and [everybooking_button] shortcodes for the Classic Editor, Elementor’s Shortcode widget and other page builders.
  • A floating quote button for every page, and #instant-quote links that turn any button into a quote button.
  • As many booking pages as you like, on as many pages as you like, including the same one more than once.
  • Your booking pages listed with pictures, to add to a new page in one click, or copy as a shortcode or button link.
  • Seven tools for AI assistants through the WordPress MCP Adapter.
  • Height, maximum width and spacing controls. Your booking page keeps its own Everybooking branding.
  • An “Open booking page” link for visitors whose browser cannot show the embedded page.

What you need

An Everybooking account with at least one published booking page. The plugin shows nothing without one. An account is free, with no credit card and no time limit; paid plans add more quotes, users and features. See pricing.

What this plugin does not do

  • It never asks for your Everybooking password. Connecting is optional and uses a connection key that can do one thing: list your published booking pages. The key cannot see bookings, customers or prices, is never shown on your website, and can be revoked in Everybooking at any time. Without a key, you paste the public link to your booking page.
  • It is not a WooCommerce integration. It does not create WooCommerce orders, carts or payments.
  • It does not include a pricing engine, an inventory database or a payment processor. Everybooking does that work.

External services

This plugin displays a page from Everybooking (everybooking.com, or your own domain if your Everybooking booking pages use one) inside an iframe. Without it the plugin shows nothing.

  • When data is sent: when a visitor opens a WordPress page that contains the block or shortcode and the booking page scrolls near view, their browser loads the booking page directly from Everybooking. A quote button loads the same booking page in the same way, only when the visitor clicks it. In the editor, the same happens when you choose “Show preview”.
  • What is sent: the visitor’s browser sends Everybooking the usual web request details (IP address, browser type) and the address of your site, without the page path. Everything the visitor then types into the booking page, such as dates, party size, contact details and payment details, goes directly from their browser to Everybooking and its payment processor. None of it passes through or is stored by WordPress or this plugin.
  • Analytics on the booking page: Everybooking’s booking pages load Everybooking’s own analytics and error monitoring (Google Analytics, Google Ads conversion measurement, Hotjar and Sentry). Mention this in your site’s privacy and cookie notices as you would for any embedded third-party service.

  • What this plugin itself sends: nothing, unless you connect it. If an administrator pastes a connection key, your WordPress server asks Everybooking for the list of that business’s published booking pages (their names and public links) when the key is saved and whenever an Everybooking block’s page picker is shown in the editor or searched. The request carries the connection key, any search text typed into the picker, and what WordPress sends with every outgoing request (your server’s IP address, and your site address and WordPress version in the User-Agent). It carries nothing about your visitors. The list includes a preview picture of each booking page; the browser of the administrator or editor looking at the list loads those pictures from where Everybooking keeps them (currently images.nice-shot.io, a screenshot service), which sees that browser’s IP address and nothing about your site. Disconnecting sends one request asking Everybooking to revoke the key. The plugin has no telemetry and adds no tracking of its own. Its AI tools (for the MCP Adapter) run inside your WordPress site and send nothing anywhere beyond the booking page list request described here.

  • The example gallery: when an administrator opens the About tab of Settings → Everybooking, your WordPress server asks everybooking.com for its public catalog of example booking pages (their names, categories, preview pictures and demo links) and keeps the answer for twelve hours. No key is involved and the request carries nothing beyond what WordPress sends with every outgoing request. The preview pictures are loaded by the administrator’s browser from where Everybooking keeps them (currently images.nice-shot.io).

Everybooking terms of service: https://everybooking.com/terms
Everybooking privacy policy: https://everybooking.com/privacy
everybooking.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. In Everybooking, go to Integrations, open WordPress, choose Create connection key and copy it.
  3. In WordPress, go to Settings → Everybooking, paste the key and choose Connect.
  4. Your booking pages appear with a preview picture of each. Star the one most visitors need as the default.
  5. Choose Add on each booking page you want on a page (the same one twice if you like), then Create draft page. Or edit a page you already have and add the Everybooking Instant Quote & Booking block or the Everybooking Quote Button block. Publish.
  6. For a quote button on every page, open the Quote buttons tab and switch on the floating button, or set the link of your theme’s own button to #instant-quote.

Prefer not to connect? Copy the link to your booking page from the same place in Everybooking (it looks like https://yourbusiness.everybooking.com/book) and paste it into the block, or save it as the default booking page under Settings → Everybooking, on the Booking pages tab.

Booking page shortcode:

[everybooking] uses the default booking page.

[everybooking url="https://yourbusiness.everybooking.com/book" height="800" max_width="900" spacing="24"]

Options: url, height (pixels, 300–4000, default 800), max_width (pixels, 280–2400, default full width), spacing (pixels above and below, 0–200), title (the name screen readers announce), link="no" (hide the “Open booking page” link).

Quote button shortcode:

[everybooking_button] opens the default booking page in a pop-up.

[everybooking_button url="https://yourbusiness.everybooking.com/rooms" text="Book a room" align="center" color="#0b3a8f"]

Options: url, text, align (left, center, right or stretch), color and text_color (like #0b3a8f), open="tab" (open the booking page in a new tab) or open="page" (go to it in the same tab) instead of the pop-up, class.

To use the plugin with an AI assistant: install the MCP Adapter plugin, make an application password under Users → Profile, and add your site to the assistant. Settings → Everybooking → Options shows the exact settings to copy.

If your booking pages are on your own domain (for example book.yourbusiness.com), add that domain under Settings → Everybooking → Options → Other booking addresses first.

Once you connect or save a default link, people who edit your site can only show booking pages from that address and any others you list under Other booking addresses. Until then, any Everybooking booking page link is accepted. If your site already shows booking pages from a different Everybooking address, add that address to the list before you connect, or those pages will stop showing.
everybooking.faq:
Can I put a “Get an Instant Quote” button on my home page?

Yes. Keep the button your theme or page builder already has and set its link to #instant-quote: clicking it opens your default booking page in a pop-up. #everybooking-your-page opens a particular booking page instead; Settings → Everybooking → Quote buttons lists the link for each of yours. Or add the Everybooking Quote Button block, or switch on the floating button.

Can I show more than one booking page?

As many as you like, on as many pages as you like, and the same one more than once. Add a block or shortcode for each, or choose Add on several booking pages in Settings → Everybooking and create a page holding them all, as booking pages or as quote buttons.

Does the pop-up work on phones?

Yes. On a phone it fills the screen, with a large close button, and the phone’s Back button closes it rather than leaving your site. If you prefer, a button can open the booking page in a new tab, or go to it in the same tab, instead of opening the pop-up.

Does it work with AI assistants like Claude or ChatGPT?

Yes, through MCP (the Model Context Protocol). Install the free MCP Adapter plugin and connect your assistant with an application password; Settings → Everybooking → Options shows how. The assistant can then list your booking pages, make pages holding any number of them, add them to existing pages, change the default and set up the quote button. It acts as the WordPress user whose password it has, so it can do only what that user can. New pages are always drafts. It needs WordPress 6.9 or newer, for the Abilities API.

Is Everybooking free?

An account is free with no credit card and no time limit, and includes 50 quotes. When you need more quotes, more users or features such as AI through MCP, there are paid plans. This plugin itself is free and has no locked features.

I have never used Everybooking. Where do I start?

After activating, open Settings → Everybooking. The page explains what Everybooking does, shows a gallery of working examples for different kinds of business that you can try, and has a button to build your free quote page. You can start from your website address or from a template for your kind of business, then come back and connect it.

What is MCP, and do I need it?

MCP (the Model Context Protocol) lets AI apps such as Claude, ChatGPT and Grok use other software for you. It is optional, and there are two separate uses. In WordPress, this plugin’s tools let an assistant place your booking pages on your site (see above). In Everybooking, on Growth plans, an assistant can build and change the booking pages themselves. Either works without the other.

Do prices and availability update automatically?

Yes. The page shown is your live Everybooking booking page, and it checks pricing and availability with Everybooking as the customer goes. This plugin caches nothing. Changes to the design or steps of a booking page appear after you publish that page again in Everybooking; this plugin never publishes or republishes anything.

Why is there a scroll bar inside the booking page?

The booking page cannot yet tell WordPress how tall it is, so it scrolls inside a frame of the height you choose. Increase the height in the block settings if you want less scrolling. On phones the frame is never taller than the screen.

Can customers come back and finish later?

Usually. Everybooking remembers a customer’s progress in their browser, so reloading the page continues where they left off. Browsers keep that memory separate for an embedded page and for the same page opened directly, and some privacy settings clear it, so a quote started on your WordPress page may not carry over to the “Open booking page” link, or the other way round.

Do personal or pre-filled links work?

Links that Everybooking sends to one customer, including pre-filled links, open on Everybooking’s own page, not inside your WordPress page. That is deliberate: a personal link must not be placed on a public page. This plugin refuses the personal link formats it can recognise, but it cannot recognise every one, so always paste the general link to your booking page, the one listed under Integrations → WordPress in Everybooking.

Does previewing in the editor create bookings?

No. The editor preview is view-only: it can be looked at but not clicked or typed into. Loading the preview does count as one visit to the booking page in Everybooking, the same as opening the page.

Who can add a booking page to my site?

Anyone who can edit pages. Changing the default link and the list of allowed addresses needs an administrator. After an administrator connects the site or saves a default link, editors can only show booking pages from your own Everybooking address.

Does it work with Elementor?

Yes, through Elementor’s Shortcode widget. There is no dedicated Elementor widget.

I use LiteSpeed Cache, WP Rocket or another speed plugin.

That is fine. The quote button’s script and styles carry the markers those plugins look for, so they are left out of “delay JavaScript”, combining and “unused CSS” removal, and the first click on a quote button always opens it. The script is small and loads deferred, so your page stays fast.

The booking page is blank or will not load.

Open the link directly in a new tab to confirm the page is published in Everybooking. Check that the link is the general link to the booking page, not a link sent to one customer. If a security plugin or header on your site sets a Content-Security-Policy, allow frames from your Everybooking address.

What happens if I remove the plugin?

The embedded booking pages disappear from your WordPress pages and the plugin’s settings, including any connection key, are deleted from WordPress. If you connected, use Disconnect first (or revoke the key in Everybooking) so the key stops working. Nothing in your Everybooking account changes: bookings, quotes and customer records are untouched.

abilityguard-mcp.description:
Tessera is a developer library for plugin authors who register abilities via wp_register_ability() and want snapshot capture, audit logging, approval workflows, and one-click rollback for every invocation across REST, MCP, internal PHP, and WP-CLI without building it themselves.

Declare what state your ability touches; Tessera handles the safety wrapper.

What you get out of the box

  • Pre + post snapshots. Every safety-enabled invocation captures declared state before the callback and (on success) after, so the audit log can show a real diff.
  • Audit log. One row per invocation with ability name, caller (REST/MCP/CLI/internal), user, args, result, status, duration, pre/post hashes, and parent_invocation_id for nested calls.
  • One-click rollback. Restore captured state from post_meta, options, taxonomy term assignments, user roles + caps. File contents support tiered drift detection (mtime / mtime_size / critical_hash / full_hash) plus opt-in real byte-level rollback via full_content strategy.
  • Drift check on rollback. Live state is hashed and compared to the snapshot’s post-state before restoring; if they differ the rollback returns an error unless forced.
  • Concurrency lock. Capture + execute is serialised per surface set via a MySQL advisory lock so two simultaneous invocations do not capture each other’s mid-states.
  • Encrypted redaction. Scrub secrets out of args, results, and snapshots. Stores redacted values as AES-256-GCM envelopes so rollback can still restore them.
  • Approval queue. When safety.requires_approval is set, the wrapper blocks execution and returns a 202 pending response. A human approves or rejects via wp-admin, WP-CLI, or REST. Multi-stage sequential or parallel approval chains are supported.
  • Multisite support. Each subsite gets its own set of wp_<N>_abilityguard_* tables, with auto-install on wp_initialize_site and auto-drop on wpmu_drop_tables.
  • Retention. Daily WP-Cron prunes old log rows (defaults: 30 days normal, 180 days destructive) and orphaned snapshots.

Surfaces

  • PHP API with wp_register_ability( $name, [ ..., 'safety' => [...] ] ) and helpers abilityguard_rollback, abilityguard_snapshot_meta, abilityguard_snapshot_options.
  • REST: /abilityguard/v1/log, /log/<id>, /log/export, /rollback/<id>, /rollback/bulk, /approval, /approval/<id>/approve, /approval/<id>/reject, /approval/bulk, /approval/export, /retention, /retention/prune, /health.
  • WP-CLI: wp abilityguard log list/show, wp abilityguard rollback <id>, wp abilityguard approval list/approve/reject <id>, wp abilityguard prune.
  • wp-admin: Tools > Tessera. Hybrid timeline + command-palette search, snapshot drawer, JSON-highlighted Input/Result tabs, invocation chain navigation, and real rollback against the captured snapshot.

Example

wp_register_ability( 'my-plugin/update-product-price', array(
    'label'               => 'Update product price',
    'description'         => 'Updates the price on a WooCommerce product.',
    'category'            => 'woocommerce',
    'input_schema'        => array( /* ... */ ),
    'permission_callback' => fn() => current_user_can( 'manage_woocommerce' ),
    'execute_callback'    => fn( $args ) => update_post_meta( $args['product_id'], '_price', $args['price'] ),
    'safety' => array(
        'destructive'       => true,
        'requires_approval' => false,
        'snapshot'          => fn( $input ) => array(
            'post_meta' => array( $input['product_id'] => array( '_price', '_regular_price' ) ),
            'options'   => array( 'woocommerce_last_price_change' ),
        ),
    ),
) );

Documentation

Full plugin-author documentation lives at the GitHub repo: https://github.com/ibrahimhajjaj/abilityguard

Source Code

The full source for Tessera, including the unminified React source for the admin app, lives on GitHub: https://github.com/ibrahimhajjaj/abilityguard

  • The admin bundle assets/admin.js is compiled from assets/admin.jsx (React + JSX, no preprocessor magic beyond JSX).
  • The bundler is esbuild, configured in scripts/build.mjs.
  • To rebuild the admin bundle from a fresh checkout, run npm install once, then npm run build whenever assets/admin.jsx changes. This regenerates assets/admin.js in place.
  • The release zip published to the WordPress.org directory is produced by scripts/build-release.sh, which excludes development artifacts (tests, examples, build configs) but keeps everything required for the plugin to run.
abilityguard-mcp.installation:
1. Upload the abilityguard-mcp folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins menu in WordPress (or network-activate on multisite).
  3. Visit Tools > Tessera to view the audit log.
  4. In your own plugin, register abilities via wp_register_ability() with a safety config.

Requires WordPress 6.9 or later (for the Abilities API) and PHP 8.1 or later.
abilityguard-mcp.faq:
Does this work without other plugins?

It will activate without registered abilities, but it only does work when other plugins register abilities with a safety config via wp_register_ability().

What state surfaces are supported for snapshots?

post_meta, options, taxonomy term assignments, user roles + caps, and files (with five tiered strategies from mtime to full content rollback).

Does it support multisite?

Yes. Each subsite gets its own set of wp_<N>_abilityguard_* tables. New subsites are auto-installed via wp_initialize_site; deleted subsites have their tables dropped via wpmu_drop_tables.

How does it handle concurrent invocations?

Per-surface MySQL advisory locks (GET_LOCK) serialise capture + execute so simultaneous invocations do not capture each other’s mid-states.

Are secrets encrypted in the log?

Yes. Redaction uses AES-256-GCM envelopes so rollback can still restore the original value when the encryption key is intact.

storeedit-ai.description:
Bulk edit WooCommerce products in plain words, with the AI assistant you already use.

StoreEdit AI connects Claude, ChatGPT or another assistant to your shop as a careful helper. You say what you want: “Raise the regular price of all shoes by 5%, except the ones on sale.” The assistant finds the products and prepares the change. Nothing is written yet. In your WordPress admin you see every product, its value now and the value it would get. You apply all of it, part of it, or none, and you can undo it later.

There is no AI model inside, no API key and no credits to buy. The assistant is yours, on your own subscription. The plugin is the safe door it works through.

How it works

  1. Ask. Tell your assistant what to change, in your own words, in any language it speaks.
  2. Review. Open the request in WordPress: what you asked, how it was understood, how many products would change, and every row with its value now and after. Untick what you do not want.
  3. Apply, and undo if you need to. Approved rows are written in the background. Undo one product or the whole request, days later if you like.

What you can change

With no limit on products or requests, and no licence:

  • Regular price and sale price, by a percentage or an amount, with sale dates
  • Stock quantity and stock status
  • Product categories: add or remove
  • Product tags: add or remove
  • Product titles, short descriptions and descriptions, each written by your assistant for that product

It works on simple and variable products: published ones by default, and drafts, pending or private ones when you ask for them.

Things you can ask

  • “Put everything in Bags on sale at 20% off until 31 October.”
  • “End the sale on all shoes that are on sale.”
  • “Set every product in Clearance to out of stock.”
  • “Add the tag new-season to every bag.”
  • “Add everything tagged gift-idea to the Gifts category as well.”
  • “Rewrite the short description of every mug so it says what it is made of and how much it holds.”

Built so that nothing goes wrong quietly

  • Nothing changes without the approval of a person who can manage the shop. The assistant cannot approve, apply or undo.
  • Every row is shown before it is written, with a tick box next to it.
  • Apply in instalments if you like: what you leave unticked waits.
  • Each row is checked again at the moment it is written. A product that changed since the preview is skipped, and you are told.
  • Undo puts back exactly what was there, for one product or for a whole request.
  • The history keeps every request: what was asked, who approved it, when, and what happened.
  • The assistant signs in with OAuth to a limited account that reads products and proposes changes. It never sees customers, orders or payments, and you can revoke its access at any time.

What it does not do

  • It does not create or delete products, and does not edit, crop or generate images.
  • It does not read or change customers, orders or shop settings.
  • It does not act on its own: no schedules, no automatic changes.

StoreEdit AI Pro

A separate, paid add-on applies the changes for which the assistant reads each product one by one: attributes, the move to the right category, SEO titles and meta descriptions (Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress, The SEO Framework), product addresses (slugs), product images and product status. Without the add-on, such a request is still planned and shown to you in full, as a preview; it is not applied. Everything under “What you can change” works without it. The add-on is at storeeditai.com.

Requirements

WordPress 7.0 or later, PHP 8.1 or later, WooCommerce, and a shop that is online over HTTPS so that your assistant can reach it. Single sites only. The screens are in English and Greek.

External services

The plugin calls no AI service and sends your catalogue nowhere on its own.

When you connect an assistant, two things happen, both started by you:

  • The assistant reads your products through the connection. The assistant you chose (for example Claude, by Anthropic, or ChatGPT, by OpenAI) asks your shop for product data: names, descriptions, prices, stock, categories, tags and attributes. It receives what it asks for, for the requests you make. It never receives customer or order data. What the assistant’s provider does with it is under that provider’s terms and privacy policy: Anthropic (terms, privacy), OpenAI (terms, privacy).
  • Images are fetched from the addresses your assistant gives. When your assistant proposes a product image, your shop downloads it from the web address the assistant named (for example your supplier’s site), to show it to you before you approve it. Only that address is requested, through WordPress’s own safe request, which refuses addresses on your own network. Like every request WordPress makes, it carries your WordPress version and your site’s address; nothing else about your shop is sent. What that site does with the request is under its own terms.
  • Sign-in reads the assistant’s public description. When an assistant starts the OAuth sign-in, your shop fetches that app’s public client metadata document from the address the app gives (for example on claude.ai or chatgpt.com), to show you its name and to check where the sign-in is sent. Only that address is requested. Like every request WordPress makes, it carries your WordPress version and your site’s address; nothing else about your shop is sent.
storeedit-ai.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce, then StoreEdit AI.
  2. Open StoreEdit AI in the WordPress menu and copy the connection address shown under “Your assistant”.
  3. In your assistant, add that address as a custom connector (a remote MCP server).
  4. Sign in to your shop when it asks, and approve the connection.
  5. Ask the assistant for a change. Then open the request in WordPress, review it and apply.
storeedit-ai.faq:
Do I need an API key, or do I pay for AI through the plugin?
